result.summary: Training gives one exact fact about N's outputs: a C x C matrix built from N's table and the labels equals lambda W W^T, so it is symmetric and positive semidefinite, and nothing more is forced at the table level (Theorems E1, E2). That fact does not decide the squeeze: two exactly stationary networks with the same lambda, W, weights, label share, entropy and cross entropy have L_free(1) = 0.0038 and 0.1475 (Theorem E3), and a certificate that uses labels stays inside a new proved limit on all duals linear in one projector, which also explains the failure of TQ18 (Proposition E5). One new exact result came from writing the loss through read moments only, and it uses no training premise: a certificate for the always-on read with no tiny probability in it, which held on tables with entries near 1e-35, where TQ18 fails by 1e30; it has no claim type, it does not cover free codes or the gated box, and I expect it to miss real networks by about 4 orders of magnitude or more (Theorem E6).

statements.statement: E1 (what stationarity forces on N's table). Premises: last hidden layer values h(x) >= 0 on P, logits l = W h + b, s = softmax(l), weights p_x, label share ebar_x in the simplex (one-hot when each input has one label), r_x = ebar_x - s_x, lambda > 0. (W, b) is stationary for CE + (lambda/2)|W|^2, with no decay on b. J = I - 11^T/C. Then: (1) sum p r = 0. (2) lambda W = sum p r h^T, and 1^T W = 0. (3) T := sum p_x r_x (J log s_x)^T = lambda W W^T. So T is symmetric and positive semidefinite, and T 1 = 0. T reads only N's outputs and the labels. (4) Trace: Hbar(s) - CE(N) = lambda |W|_F^2, for one-hot labels. So N is less confident on P than its own CE, by exactly this amount, and lambda |W|^2 <= log C with no other premise. (5) Per unit u, with M_u = sum p h_u: lambda w_u = M_u (label share under u's firing - mean s under u's firing), and -sum p s[i] h_u <= lambda W_iu <= sum p ebar[i] h_u. Per class, for one-hot labels: lambda W[i,:] = pi_i (mu_i - mutilde_i), with mu_i the label mean of h and mutilde_i the s[i]-weighted mean of h. (6) l_x = b + (1/lambda) sum over x' of p_x' r_x' <h(x), h(x')>. (7) rank T = rank W = affine rank of the logit table, so L_free(k) = 0 exactly when rank T <= k. (8) At a stationary triple on heads of h, with Gamma = sum p (s - q) h^T: Gamma = sum p (e - q) h^T - lambda W; lambda V^T W = V^T sum p (e - q) h^T; lambda <W, W_b> = Hbar(q) - CE(q). If b also has decay: sum p r = lambda b, and T = lambda (W W^T + b b^T).
statements.proof: (1), (2) are the gradient in b and W. 1^T r_x = 0 gives lambda 1^T W = 0. (3) J log s_x = J l_x = W h_x + J b, since W^T 1 = 0 and softmax differs from l by a constant times 1. T = sum p r h^T W^T + (sum p r)(Jb)^T = lambda W W^T. (4) tr T = sum p <r, log s> because 1^T r = 0, and <e_y - s, log s> = log s[y] + H(s). Sum over x. Take traces in (3). H <= log C and CE >= 0 give the bound. (5) Multiply (2) on column u. Use h_u >= 0 and r_x[i] in [-s_x[i], ebar_x[i]]. Mean-share equality (1) gives the same pi_i in both means. (6) Substitute (2) into l. (7) J l_x - J b = W h_x, so affine rank <= rank W. By (1), T = sum p r (J l - J b)^T, so rank T <= affine rank. And rank T = rank W by (3). A positive table has a least that is attained, and it is 0 exactly when logits mod 1 have affine rank <= k. (8) Subtract in the definition; apply V^T Gamma = 0; apply <Gamma, W_b> = 0 and sum p (e - q) = sum p (s - q) = 0, and <e_y - q, l_b> = log q[y] + H(q). With decay on b, (1) changes to lambda b, and 1^T b = 0; repeat (3).

statements.statement: E2 (the converse: E1 is all that stationarity forces at the table). Let s be a positive table on rows with weights p, label shares ebar_x, r_x = ebar_x - s_x, and T as in E1. Assume (a) sum p r = 0, (b) T symmetric positive semidefinite, (c) some bhat has J log s_x - bhat in range(T) for all x. Then for every lambda > 0 and every m >= 1 there is a ReLU network with m hidden layers (decay lambda on weights, none on biases, every unit on at every row) that is exactly stationary, outputs s_x on each row, has these label shares, and has W W^T = T / lambda. Hard labels on distinct inputs are allowed: one row is split into many inputs, each with one label. At m = 1 the network is a local minimum of the objective and the global least among all-on networks of any width. Corollary (soft labels): for any positive table, any p, and any symmetric positive semidefinite Gamma whose range is the row space of L (L = rows J log s_x minus their unweighted mean), the shares ebar_x = s_x + (lambda/p_x) Gamma (L^T L)^+ L_x give T = lambda Gamma, valid for lambda <= lambda_0 = least over x, i of p_x s_x[i] / [-(Gamma (L^T L)^+ L_x)_i]_+ > 0. So: being stationary for some labels excludes no positive table, and W's spectrum is free relative to the table, apart from its range. Only lambda W W^T in a convex compact set T(s, p) is forced. For one-hot labels on K = C class rows the condition has bite: C(C-1)/2 equations on C(C-1) table numbers. For n >> C rows, it is weak.
statements.proof: Write T = Q Lambda Q^T on its range, Gamma = Lambda / lambda, L_x = J log s_x - bhat. By (a), T = sum p r L^T. Set W = Q Gamma^(1/2), U_j = Gamma^(1/2) (r x r), inputs phi_x = Gamma^(-(m+1)/2) Q^T L_x. Then W U_m ... U_1 phi_x = Q Q^T L_x = L_x by (c). Large biases beta_j keep all units on; the shift is undone by b. Sum p r phi^T = T Q Gamma^(-(m+1)/2) = Q Lambda Gamma^(-(m+1)/2). The CE gradient in U_j is minus Gamma^((m-j+1)/2) Lambda Gamma^(-(m+1)/2) Gamma^((j-1)/2) = minus Lambda Gamma^(-1/2) = minus lambda Gamma^(1/2) = minus lambda U_j. The head gives lambda W in the same way. The gradients in the biases are sums of r against constants, 0 by (a). Hard labels: for row x and class i add inputs (phi_x, +e_(x,i)) and (phi_x, -e_(x,i)), each with weight p_x ebar_x[i] / 2 and label i, on new coordinates with zero weights; the moments on these coordinates cancel. m = 1: near this point units stay on, so logits are B phi + const with B = W U, and |W|^2 + |U|^2 >= 2 |B|_*. F(B, c) = CE + lambda |B|_* is convex. At B = Q Gamma, the negative CE gradient is sum p r phi^T = lambda Q, the top singular factors of B times lambda, so 0 is a subgradient. So R >= F >= F* = R at this point. Corollary: sum p r = lambda Gamma (L^T L)^+ sum L_x = 0, and T = lambda Gamma (L^T L)^+ L^T L = lambda Gamma. (c) holds by the range premise.

statements.statement: E3 (training-forced numbers do not decide the squeeze). Premises: C = 3, n = 4, p_x = 1/4, A an orthonormal basis of 1^perp, epsilon in (0, 1]. Table A_eps has rows softmax(b + A xi) with xi = (+-3, +-eps). Table B has rows xi = (+-m, +-m), with m chosen so Hbar(B) = Hbar(A_eps). b is chosen in each table so that the mean of s is uniform. Then for each eps there is lambda_eps > 0 such that both tables are outputs of exactly stationary 2-layer ReLU networks with hard labels on distinct inputs, each a local minimum, sharing lambda, W = A, U = I, p, label share, mean of s, Hbar and CE. And L_free(1; A_eps) <= eps^2 / 4, while L_free(1; B) >= c_0 > 0 with c_0 independent of eps. So for any function F of (lambda, W W^T, p, label share, Hbar, CE): if F >= L_free(1), then F / L_free(1) >= 4 c_0 / eps^2, unbounded on A_eps; if F <= L_free(1), then F <= eps^2 / 4 on B. No bound in these numbers alone is first-order tight. The same holds with any Gamma on one fixed table: by E2's Corollary the singular value sigma_(k+1)(W) can go to 0 while the table and L_free(k) stay fixed. Trained-like, said plainly: labels are noisy on inputs with equal outputs, as at train accuracy below 100%. It does not cover one-hot labels with one class per row at K = C, where (E2) T has bite.
statements.proof: Existence of b: the mean softmax is the gradient of a coercive strictly convex function modulo constants, onto the interior of the simplex. Stationarity: E2's Corollary with Gamma = I on 1^perp, so L = xi A^T, columns centred, T = lambda (I - 11^T/3), W = A. lambda_eps = min of the two lambda_0, both positive. CE = Hbar - lambda |W|^2 = Hbar - 2 lambda by E1(4), so CE agrees. m exists: Hbar(B_m) is continuous, goes to log 3 as m -> 0 and to 0 as m -> infinity. Hbar(A_eps) stays in a compact part of (0, log 3) for eps in [0, 1], so the roots m stay in a compact interval. Upper bound on A_eps: competitor b + (+-3) A e_1 has rank 1, and the logit difference d = +-eps A e_2 has osc <= sqrt(2) eps, so Hoeffding's lemma gives KL <= osc^2 / 8 = eps^2 / 4 at each row. Lower bound on B: logits have affine rank 2, so L_free(1) > 0; it is continuous on positive tables, so it has a positive least on the compact m interval. Last sentence: E2's Corollary with Gamma = diag(1, ..., 1, sigma^2): T = lambda Gamma, table unchanged, with lambda <= lambda_0.

statements.statement: E4 (a rank bound from lambda and W alone, valid but far from tight). Premises: E1 with sum p r = 0. Let E_k = sum over i > k of sigma_i(W)^2, s_x^min the least entry of row x, tau_0 = least over x of s_x^min / |r_x|_2, kappa = sum p_x |r_x|^2 / s_x^min. Then for every k <= C - 2: V_b(k) >= L_Z(k) >= L_free(k) >= min{ (lambda E_k)^2 / (4 kappa), tau_0 lambda E_k / 2 }. For every competitor with complement projector Pi: sum p_x <Pi r_x, log s_x - l'_x> = lambda |Pi W|_F^2 >= lambda E_k. Minors: for a class set H, with s_x(H) the mass of H and s^H the conditional, u_x = (e_x|H - s_x|H) / s_x(H): the first-order term in the minor is exactly lambda |Pi_H W_H|_F^2 >= lambda E_k(J_H W_H), with no leak term, so the same form holds with tau_H = least of s^H_min / |u_x| and kappa_H = sum p_x s_x(H) |u_x|^2 / s^H_min; then TQ22 adds these over disjoint H. Failure, said plainly: bound over truth was 1e-2 to 1e-5 on tiny tables, and 1/s^min makes it empty at real tables.
statements.proof: Fix a competitor (t', V', c'). Pi is the projector onto the complement of 1 and V'. q_x = s_x - tau Pi r_x. |Pi r_x|_inf <= |r_x|_2, so q_x is a distribution when tau <= tau_0. Pi V' = 0, Pi 1 = 0, and sum p Pi r = 0 kill the terms of TQ13 part 1 in c', 1 and t'. So D >= sum p (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) = tau sum p <log s_x, Pi r_x> - sum p KL(q_x || s_x) = tau tr(Pi T) - sum p KL. tr(Pi T) = lambda |Pi W|^2 >= lambda E_k by Ky Fan, since Pi has rank C - 1 - k in 1^perp and W^T 1 = 0. KL <= chi^2 <= tau^2 |r_x|^2 / s_x^min. Choose tau. Minors: same with q^H_x = s^H_x - tau Pi_H u_x; log s^H_x = l_x|H + const; sum p_x s_x(H) <log s^H_x, Pi_H u_x> = sum p_x <l_x|H, Pi_H r_x|H> = lambda tr(Pi_H W_H W_H^T); balance holds since sum p_x s_x(H) u_x = (sum p r)|H = 0.

statements.statement: E5 (the limit of any dual point linear in one projector). Premises: C >= 4, a positive row s, a fixed vector u in 1^perp, and the dual family q(Pi) = s - Pi u, required to be a distribution for every orthogonal projector Pi of rank m, 1 <= m <= C - 3, with Pi 1 = 0. Then |u|_2 <= 2 s_(2) / ((1 - 1/sqrt 2) (1 - 1/C)^(1/2)), which is at most 8.4 s_(2), with s_(2) the second smallest entry of s. So if a triple is certified by such a family, with equality at its own projector, then |s_x - q_x|_2 <= 8.4 s_x,(2) on every row. This covers Theorems TQ17 and TQ18, at Z = R^n, and every choice of the row vector u_x, including label residuals. So labels cannot rescue this class. A row with entries of 1e-12 allows a residual of about 1e-11. It explains why level tails were the only family: there s_(2) is the tail level.
statements.proof: Let a = J e_i, |a|^2 = 1 - 1/C, and t_i the cosine of a and u. Take w the unit bisector of a and u, plus m - 1 unit vectors orthogonal to a, u, 1 (room exists since m <= C - 3). Then a^T Pi u = (a.w)(u.w) = (1/2) |a||u| (1 + t_i). Requiring entry i of q(Pi) >= 0 gives (1/2)|a||u|(1 + t_i) <= s_i for each i. For two classes a, b with unit vectors a^, b^: a^.b^ = -1/(C-1), so t_a + t_b >= -|a^ + b^| >= -sqrt 2, so the larger of 1 + t_a, 1 + t_b is at least 1 - 1/sqrt 2. Apply to the two smallest entries.

statements.statement: E6 (moment certificate for a read: rho is replaced by an average Fisher number). This uses no training premise. Setting: rows with p_x > 0, positive s_x. Z has a p-orthonormal basis zeta_x in R^D (sum p zeta zeta^T = I), first coordinates spanning Y, with 1 in Y; zeta has full column rank. Competitors: l'_x = B' zeta_x with B' = [A', V' M'] and V' of rank at most k. L_Z(k) is the least. Triple: q_x = softmax(B_0 zeta_x), B_0 = [A_0, V M_0], V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, M_0 of rank k, sigma its least singular value, C >= k + 2, k* = min(k, C-1-k). Stationary: Gamma_0 = sum p (s - q) zeta^T has zero Y part, and its other part Gamma satisfies V^T Gamma = 0, Gamma M_0^T = 0. g = |Gamma|_op. Psi(B) = sum p Cov(q_x) B zeta_x zeta_x^T on {B: 1^T B = 0}, self-adjoint, eta its least eigenvalue, zeta_max = largest |zeta_x|. Then eta > 0, and: (1) If g <= eta sigma / 2 and 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max <= eta, the triple is a global least: L_Z(k) = sum p (H(q) - H(s)). (2) If only 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max <= eta: D(triple) - L_Z(k) <= k* g (2 g / eta - sigma)_+. (3) The test reads s only through Gamma_0. So adding to s any delta with sum p delta zeta^T = 0 that keeps it positive changes neither the test nor the triple's status; what the read cannot compute costs nothing here, however large it is, and s may have tiny entries. Scope, plainly: at Z = R^n, eta is a per-row minimum, about the least probability, and TQ18 returns, so it gives nothing new for free codes. It covers the always-on read and region tables with K >> dim Z, not the gated box: V_b <= L_on, so it does not give V(G) by itself. Labelled proved matching lower bound for L_on only.
statements.proof: (a) eta > 0: if Var over q_x of B zeta_x is 0 at every row, then B zeta_x is in R 1, since q_x > 0; with 1^T B = 0 this gives B zeta_x = 0 at all rows, so B = 0. (b) Fix a competitor. Pi is the projector onto the complement of 1 and V' (extend if needed), rank m = C - 1 - k; Pi_0 likewise for V; E = Pi - Pi_0; X = tr(V^T Pi V) <= k*; |E|_F^2 = 2 X, as in TQ18. Let Btil = M_0^T (M_0 M_0^T)^-1, w = g sigma, R = Gamma + w V Btil^T. Then Pi_0 R = Gamma, and |R|_op = g: left spaces are orthogonal by V^T Gamma = 0, right spaces by Gamma M_0^T = 0. (c) Let B_E = Psi^-1 of the matrix with zero Y part and other part -E R (it lies in the domain since 1^T E = 0). f_x = B_E zeta_x, g_x = f_x - <q_x, f_x> 1, q°_x = q_x (1 + g_x) = q_x + Cov(q_x) f_x. Row entries sum to 1. |B_E|_F <= |E R|_F / eta <= g sqrt(2 X) / eta, and osc(f_x) <= sqrt 2 |f_x|_2 <= 2 sqrt(k*) g |zeta_x| / eta <= 1, so q° >= 0. (d) Feasibility: sum p (q° - s) zeta^T = (sum p (q° - q) zeta^T) - Gamma_0, with Y part 0 and other part -E R - Gamma = -Pi R, since Pi_0 R = Gamma. So V'^T annihilates it, and <its matrix, B'> = 0. TQ13 part 1 at each row gives D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)). (e) H(q°) - H(q) = -<log q, q° - q> - KL(q° || q). log q_x = B_0 zeta_x - (log Z_x) 1 and q° - q is orthogonal to 1. So the linear term is <B_0, the other part E R> = tr(M_0^T V^T E Gamma) + w tr(M_0^T V^T E V Btil^T) = 0 + w tr(V^T E V) = w X, using Gamma M_0^T = 0, V^T Pi_0 = 0, Btil^T M_0^T = I. (f) (1 + y) log(1 + y) <= y + y^2 for y >= -1, with E_q g = 0, gives sum p KL <= sum p Var_q(f) = <B_E, Psi B_E> = <E R, Psi^-1 E R> <= 2 X g^2 / eta. (g) So D(l') >= sum p (H(q) - H(s)) + X g (sigma - 2 g / eta). At stationarity sum p <q - s, log q> = 0, so D(triple) = sum p (H(q) - H(s)). (1), (2) follow with X <= k*. (3): delta changes neither Gamma_0 nor q°, and H(s) cancels on both sides. Same-form note: Z = R^n has zeta_x = e_x / sqrt(p_x), and Psi is a block per row, with the test of TQ18 in the first condition.

statements.check: e_arg.py, which tests the argument: 40 random competitors from near to far, C = 6, D = 6, k = 2, at g up to 30 times the test's cap. q° never negative, moments 1e-17, identity D0 + w X - KL to 1e-16, KL - Var <= 0 always, D(best at V') >= bound always, bound >= D0 + X g (sigma - 2 g / eta) always, and never below D0. statements.statement: E6-reach (expected, not proved, for any rank of Gamma; proved only for rank r <= 2 k*). Let Delta_k = L_Z(k) - L_Z(C-1) and r = rank Gamma. Under E6's test, Delta_k <= r g^2 / eta <= r eta / (4 k* zeta_max^2) <= r / (4 k* D (C-1)). On ResNet-18, C = 1000, D = about 513, r about 499, k = 14, this is about 1.7e-5 nats; at k = 128 it is about 1.5e-6 nats. The real cost of rank at k = 14 is of order 1 nat. So I expect the operator-norm test to miss real networks by 4 orders of magnitude or more, far better than TQ18's 1e23 to 1e78 but still a miss.

statements.check: The parts proved: eta <= 1/(C-1), since the trace of Psi is sum p tr Cov(q_x) |zeta_x|^2 < D on a space of dimension (C-1) D. zeta_max^2 >= D, since the p-mean of |zeta|^2 is D. Delta_k <= <F, Psi F> with Psi F = Gamma when |F zeta_x| keeps q positive, which the test gives only for r <= 2 k*. Otherwise this is second order. The numbers for ResNet-18 are arithmetic from the stated C, D and k, not a measurement.

statements.statement: E7 (the relation with the read that training does not give). Failed target: a relation between residual and always-on read z. What holds: lambda W = sum p r h^T with h = relu(z), and lambda u_u = sum p <r, w_u> D_u(x) h_2(x) with the gate D_u. So stationarity speaks only on a unit's on-side. Proposition: let rows x+ and x- have equal weight, the same active set A, the same values on A, labels with shares s + rho and s - rho, and rho orthogonal to the range of W on A. Then all stationarity equations are unchanged, the table is unchanged, and the always-on moment sum p r z_u^T changes by p rho (z_u(x+) - z_u(x-)), with size free. In addition: if a layer's weights theta are followed by a normalisation that makes outputs invariant under theta -> alpha theta (BatchNorm, LayerNorm), then <theta, grad CE> = 0, so stationarity lambda theta = -grad CE gives theta = 0. So on real ResNets, F8's exact stationarity can hold only at the head, and P must be the augmented training list. Heads on h: TQ12 part 4 makes the D least a ridge-tilted R least; the rank constraint is the same nonconvex object, so that is a relabelling. A head on h adds a layer, as TQ12's Comment says.
statements.proof: Proposition: both rows have the same h, so moments against h cancel between them: p rho h - p rho h = 0. (2) Every member of TQ17's family at t = 0 and uniform pi has T symmetric positive semidefinite, so by E2 it is the output of an exactly stationary network with one label per class, for every lambda. Its residual is a label step: s_c - q_c = kappa Pi* (e_c - q_c), kappa = mu_c / (1 - alpha - beta), with alpha, beta the q values on c and c'. statements.proof: (1) S and L^c lie in the commutative tree algebra, with common eigenspaces. On the contrasts of height h, S has eigenvalue sigma_h < 1 (positive stochastic symmetric, nonconstant vector), and L has xi_h = sum over j < h of n_j a_j - 2^(h-1) a_h = sum over j < h of n_j (a_j - a_h). T = (1/C)(I - S) L^c has eigenvalue (1 - sigma_h) xi_h / C. So T is symmetric, and positive semidefinite exactly when all xi_h >= 0; (c) of E2 holds because T and L^c have the same nonzero eigenspaces. (2) In the pair algebra (I, P_s, 11^T): on e_c - e_c', xi = log(alpha_s / beta_s) > 0. On pair-symmetric contrasts, xi = log(alpha_s beta_s) - 2 log gamma_s. With q q' = q''^2 at t = 0, and s adding a > 0 to q, q' and subtracting b > 0 from q'': (q + a)(q' + a) > q q' = q''^2 > (q'' - b)^2, so xi > 0. result.summary: Proved: k units can share any number J of relative families, with relatives on one graded pole and top class at 0.9 to 0.99, and the least is a closed form at a loss of 0.5 to 8 times the tail mass (Theorem D2), while whole-table TQ18 misses these tables by 1e43 to 1e270. The proof is new where it goes beyond TQ17 and TQ22: a K = 3, k = 1 theorem by a sum over rows, and a composition theorem whose dual point uses one local projector per patch of the table, which contains TQ17, TQ18 and TQ22 plus TQ18 as cases. Row 3 is not closed: only Slot 3 is filled, the exact class has almost no cost of sharing units in its stranger rows, while real networks hold most of their fine-scale loss there, and the kept-attribute build of a product table stops being the least near tanh b = a e^(-2a).

statements.statement: Theorem D1 (three classes, one unit, a confident table). Let K = C = 3, pi_c = 1/3, s_c = a on class c and b on the others, a > b > 0, a + 2b = 1. Let e be the root in (0, min(b, a/4)) of (a - 4e) sqrt((a - e)(b - e)) = (b + 2e)^2. Write A1 = a - e, m = b + 2e, beta = b - e, A2 = a - 4e, mu = 6e, tau = (1/2) log(A1/beta). Then L_table(1) = (1/3)[2 H(A1, m, beta) + H(m, A2, m)] - H(a, b, b), and this is above 0, at every a. The build has v = (1, 0, -1), codes (tau, 0, -tau), offset (0, t2, 0), t2 = log(A2/m). The spans of minimisers, modulo 1, are exactly the three line spans, one for each choice of middle class.
statements.proof:
Root: on [0, min(b, a/4)] the left side falls from a positive value to 0 and the right side rises from b^2 to a positive value, so the root is unique. Build: q_1 = (A1, m, beta), q_2 = (m, A2, m), q_3 = (beta, m, A1). The root equation is exactly the statement that these three rows have the logits of the build. Also s_c - q_c = mu Pi* e_c, with Pi* = n* n*^T, n* = (1, -2, 1)/sqrt 6.
Competitor: fix (t', v', y'). Take a unit n' orthogonal to 1 and v', and write n' = cos(theta) n* + sin(theta) vhat, vhat = (1, 0, -1)/sqrt 2. Let Pi = n' n'^T, E = Pi - Pi*, Refl = 2 Pi* - J, and let the partner map be 1 -> 3, 2 -> 2, 3 -> 1. Let q°_c = s_c - mu Pi Refl J e_(*c). The direct computation gives q°_c = q_c - mu f_c with f_1 = (u, w, -T), f_2 = (w, -T, u), f_3 = (-T, u, w), where T = (2/3) sin^2(theta), u = T/2 + sin(theta) cos(theta) / sqrt 3, w = T/2 - sin(theta) cos(theta) / sqrt 3. So u + w = T and u^2 + w^2 = T - T^2, hence u, w <= 1/2. Entries are positive: A1 - mu x >= A2, m - mu x >= beta for x <= 1/2. Feasibility: each row of q° - s kills 1 and v', and the rows sum to 0, since the partner map is a bijection. So part 1 of TQ13 gives D(competitor) >= mean H(q°) - H(s).
Expansion by (E) of TQ17 gives 3 (mean H(q°) - mean H(q)) = Z(T) = mu T Gamma - sum over x in {u, w} of [A1 phi(-mu x/A1) + 2 m phi(-mu x/m)] - 2 beta phi(mu T/beta) - A2 phi(mu T/A2), with Gamma = log(A1 m^2 / (beta^2 A2)). The root equation says m^2 = A2 sqrt(A1 beta), so Gamma = 3 tau.
For r > 0 and x <= 1/2 the monotone ratio phi(y)/y^2 gives r phi(-mu x/r) <= 4 r phi(-mu/(2r)) x^2. So Z(T) >= G(T) = 3 mu tau T - gamma (T - T^2) - 2 beta phi(mu T/beta) - A2 phi(mu T/A2), gamma = 4 A1 phi(-mu/(2 A1)) + 8 m phi(-mu/(2 m)).
Now mu/2 = 3e gives 1 + mu/(2 beta) = m/beta, 1 + mu/(2 A2) = A1/A2, 1 - mu/(2 A1) = A2/A1, 1 - mu/(2 m) = beta/m. Substituting: G'(1/2) = mu (3 tau - Gamma) = 0 and G(1/2) = 3 e (3 tau - Gamma) = 0. G(0) = 0. G''' = 2 mu^3 / (beta + mu T)^2 + mu^3 / (A2 + mu T)^2 > 0. The interpolation remainder at nodes 0, 1/2, 1/2 gives G(T) = G'''(z) T (T - 1/2)^2 / 6 >= 0 on [0, 2/3]. Equality needs T in {0, 1/2}, so theta in {0, 60, 120 degrees}, which are the three lines. QED.

statements.statement:
Theorem D2 (family pole tables: k units, any number of families, relatives on one graded pole). Let the C classes be split into families H_1, ..., H_J of size K, with K = 2k and k >= 2, or K = 3 and k = 1. Rows: one region per class, weights p_c > 0. Let (t, V, c) be a rank-k build with q_c = softmax(t + V c_c) such that, for c in H_j, the logits on H_j equal a constant plus t^(j) + tau_j (e_c - e_c'), where c' is c's partner in a fixed pairing of H_j (for K = 3: logits tau_j s_c s' plus (0, t2_j, 0), with s in {+1, 0, -1}). Write w_c = p_c q_c(H_j), qhat_c = q_c conditioned on H_j. Let the table s_c equal q_c off H_j, have s_c(H_j) = q_c(H_j), and on H_j have the conditional shat_c, where (w on H_j, t^(j), tau_j, mu_j) is in the pole family of DQ13 and shat_c = qhat_c + (mu_j / w_c) Pi* e_c (for K = 3: w uniform on H_j and shat the symmetric table of D1). Then:
1. L_free(k) = L_table(k) = the sum over j, c in H_j of w_c (H(qhat_c) - H(shat_c)), and this is above 0.
2. Such builds exist with any J. For k >= 2: take unit vectors mu_j with mu_j . mu_j' <= 1 - Delta, 0 < delta <= sqrt(Delta) / (2 sqrt 2), A >= 4 sqrt(2) tau / (delta sqrt(Delta)). For class (j, a, s), s = +-1: u = mu_j + delta s e_a, code = A mu_j + (tau/delta) s e_a, t = -delta s A mu_j[a]. Then each stranger's odds against the row's top class are at most exp(-A Delta / 4). For k = 1: v = mu_j + delta s, code A mu_j + s tau/delta, t = -A mu_j^2/2 - A mu_j delta s + t^(j)_s, with |mu_j - mu_j'| = g >= 4 delta, A g >= 8 tau/delta. Then a stranger's logit is at most tau + t2 - A g^2/8 above the row's constant.
3. If |mu_j[a]| > delta for every a, all relatives have one sign on every unit, with graded values mu_j[a] - delta, mu_j[a], mu_j[a] + delta. So each pole holds relatives, in many families.
4. (Group = circuit.) If moreover z_S is constant on each region, and the region means with a constant are independent, then V_b(k) = L_on(k) = L_free(k), by TQ14 part 6.
statements.proof:
(1) Upper side: the chain rule over the partition into H_j and the single classes outside it, with equal block masses and equal entries outside, gives KL(s_c || q_c) = q_c(H_j) KL(shat_c || qhat_c). TQ17 part 1 (or D1) gives the sum of w_c KL(shat_c || qhat_c) = the sum of w_c (H(qhat_c) - H(shat_c)). Lower side: apply TQ22 with R_b = the rows of family b and H_b = H_b. The minor b has weights p_c s_c(H_b) = w_c and table shat. Its least with k units is exactly the table least of TQ17 (K = 2k) or D1 (K = 3). So L_free(k) >= the sum of the minors' leasts, which equals the upper side. L_table = L_free by TQ14 part 4.
(2) Direct expansion. For k >= 2, row (j, a, s), class (j'', a'', s'') in the same family: t + u . code = A + (tau/delta) s mu_j[a] + tau s s'' [a'' = a], since the two terms in delta s'' A mu_j[a''] cancel. That is the block form with t^(j) = 0. For a stranger class (j', a', s'), the logit minus the row's top logit is -A Delta' + (tau/delta) s (mu_j'[a] - mu_j[a]) + delta s' A (mu_j[a'] - mu_j'[a']) + tau (s s' [a' = a] - 1), with Delta' = 1 - mu_j . mu_j' >= Delta and |mu_j - mu_j'| = sqrt(2 Delta'). The premises bound the second and third terms by A Delta'/4 and A Delta'/2. The k = 1 case is the same computation with -A g^2/2 + delta A g <= -A g^2/4 and (tau/delta) g <= A g^2/8.
(3) Read from the form of u. (4) TQ14 part 6 with the closed form. QED.

A claim names a partition A_c of P with one region per class, a partition of the classes into families of size K, a pairing in each family, and numbers (t^(j), tau_j, mu_j). With pi_c, sbar_c as in DQ10, w_c = pi_c sbar_c(H_j), qhat_c = softmax(t^(j) + tau_j (e_c - e_c')), shat_c = qhat_c + (mu_j / w_c) Pi* e_c, form the matrix Lambda: Lambda_(c, i) = log sbar_c[i] for i outside c's family, and log(sbar_c(H_j) qhat_c[i]) inside it. If the error is 0: Lambda has double-centred rank at most k, so Lambda = t + V c + (a row constant) 1. Each row of exp(Lambda) sums to the sum of sbar_c outside H_j plus sbar_c(H_j), which is 1. So softmax(t + V c_c) = exp(Lambda_c), which is a build with the block form and with the table's masses. The other direction is direct. QED.

Theorem D3 (the patchwork certificate: a dual point with one local projector per patch). Let rows x carry p_x, s_x, and let l_x = t + V c_x be a rank-k build, q_x = softmax(l_x), G = D_p(S - Q). A patch b is a set of rows R_b, a set of classes H_b with |H_b| >= k + 2, and matrices G_b on R_b x H_b with sum over b of G_b = G. Let L_b be the block of l, doubly centred, assumed of rank exactly k. Assume G_b 1 = 0, 1^T G_b = 0, G_b L_b^T = 0, L_b^T G_b = 0. Choose shares w_b >= 0 on R_b x H_b, with sum over b of w_b[x, i] <= p_x q_x[i]. For a competitor, let Pi_b be a projector of rank |H_b| - 1 - k on R^(H_b), with Pi_b killing 1 and V' restricted to H_b. Let Phi_b(Pi_b) be matrices on R_b x H_b with Phi_b 1 = 0, 1^T Phi_b = 0, and (G_b + Phi_b) killing 1 and V' on H_b. If for every Pi_b: Val_b = <Phi_b, l> - sum over x, i of w_b[x, i] phi(-Phi_b[x, i] / w_b[x, i]) >= 0, with all arguments >= -1, then L_free(k) = D(build) = the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)).
Test Q gives Val_b >= 0. Take a positive vector eta on H_b, summing to 1. Whiten: Gt = G_b D_eta^(-1/2). Let Ut be an orthonormal basis of the k-dimensional whitened span, Pi0 the projector onto the complement of D_eta^(1/2) 1 and Ut, Pi_eta the same for the competitor. Let r_x = min over i of w_b[x, i] / eta_i, rt_x = min over i of w_b[x, i] / sqrt(eta_i), and ct the row codes in Ut. Let B be any matrix with 1^T B = 0 and ct^T B = I. Test Q: some w >= 0 has |Gt_x|^2 + w^2 |B_x|^2 <= rt_x^2 for every x, and 2 |D_r^(-1/2) (Gt Gt^T + w^2 B B^T) D_r^(-1/2)|_op <= w.
Test F is Theorem D4 below, applied inside the patch.
statements.proof:
Let G° = sum over b of (G_b + Phi_b) and q°_x = s_x - G°_x / p_x = q_x - (sum over b of Phi_b[x]) / p_x. Row sums are 1. On each patch G_b + Phi_b kills 1 and V', and its columns sum to 0 (1^T G_b = 0, 1^T Phi_b = 0), so the sum over x of p_x <q°_x - s_x, t' + V' c'_x> = 0. Weak duality (part 1 of TQ13) gives D(competitor) >= the sum of p_x (H(q°_x) - H(s_x)). By (E) of TQ17, the sum of p_x (H(q°_x) - H(q_x)) = the sum over b of <Phi_b, l> - the sum over x, i of p_x q_x[i] phi(d / q_x[i]), with d = -(sum over b of Phi_b[x, i]) / p_x, since rows of Phi_b sum to 0. The map (w, y) -> w phi(y / w) is the perspective of a convex function, so it is jointly convex and homogeneous, hence subadditive: p q phi(d / q) <= the sum over b of w_b phi(-Phi_b / w_b), and the leftover share carries y = 0 and costs 0. The same subadditivity gives q + d >= 0 from the arguments >= -1. So D(competitor) >= the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) + the sum over b of Val_b. Finally D(build) = the sum of p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) - <G, l>, and <G_b, l> = <G_b, L_b> = 0, because G_b has zero row and column sums and is orthogonal to L_b.

statements.statement: Theorem D4 (the reflection certificate: TQ17's row identity holds for every build). Let V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, Pi0 = J - V V^T of rank m = C - 1 - k >= 1, u_i = V^T e_i, Refl = 2 Pi0 - J. Let * map rows to classes, with kappa_x > 0, such that: (a) the sum of kappa_x over rows with partner i is the same number kappabar for every class i; (b) the sum over x of kappa_x c_x e_(*x)^T Pi0 = 0; (c) Xi = - the sum over x of kappa_x c_x u_(*x)^T has symmetric part with least eigenvalue lam > 0. Let tau_e = lam / (2 kappabar), mu_x = kappa_x / p_x, q'_x = q_x[*x], m_x = the least of q_x[i] over i != *x, and s_x = q_x + mu_x Pi0 e_(*x). Let K = C = 4, k = 1, p uniform, s_(alpha, beta)(alpha', beta') proportional to exp(a alpha alpha' + b beta beta'), a, b > 0. Let eps = e^(-a) / (2 cosh a), sigma = 1 - eps, T = tanh b, kept(b) = log 2 - h((1 + T)/2). 1. The build that keeps attribute 1 is stationary with loss kept(b), and L_free(1) = kept(b) if T <= eps min(1/2, a). 2. For every eta > 0, with xi = a b / eta, the logits a alpha alpha' + b beta beta' + xi beta' (alpha - alpha') + eta beta alpha' are rank 1 plus an offset, and they have the exact loss B(eta) = log sigma + (1/2) log[(1 + (eps/sigma) e^(-2 eta) (cosh 2xi + T sinh 2xi)) (1 + (eps/sigma) e^(2 eta) (cosh 2xi - T sinh 2xi))]. 3. So L_free(1) <= (eps/sigma) [(1 - T) sinh^2(2 sqrt(a b)) + eps]. Hence kept(b) is not the least once T^2 / 2 exceeds that bound. For a b <= 1/4 and a >= 1/2 this holds when T is above about 11 a eps. 4. The two thresholds differ by a factor of about 22 a. result.summary: I did not prove a full impossibility, and I did not prove NP-hardness: L_table(k) at fixed size is continuous in the table, so a true jump does not exist there, and my hardness attempt stops at one named step. What I did prove for N: if photos are confident and the tail is thin, even one unit can write the table, but moving 2e of probability into a graded tail (a change of at most 2e in L1 per row) raises the least by at least (1-4e)/16 nats on large enough tables, so no bound in a table-distance error can be size-free, while a bound in the largest log-ratio error is size-free. I also proved a sharp threshold for rows confident on m+1 classes (2m+1 units are enough as the tail goes to 0, and at 2m units a floor holds at any tail depth), plus a first floor that charges for sharing units across strangers, with constants far too weak for real networks.

statements.statement: F1 (no jump in the table at fixed size). Fix rows, weights p, C, k and a code class Z. Extend D to rows on the closed simplex (0 log 0 = 0). Let psi(s) = inf over logits l of the class of the sum of p_x [A(l_x) - <s_x, l_x>], with A = log-sum-exp. Then psi is concave and finite on the product of closed simplices, L_Z(k)(s) = psi(s) - sum of p_x H(s_x), and L_Z(k) is continuous in s on the whole closed product, tails at 0 included. It is at least the sum of p_x H(s_x) >= 0 and finite, since KL(s||q) = A(l) - <s, l> - H(s) >= 0. A concave function on a polytope is lower semicontinuous (Rockafellar, Convex Analysis, Theorem 10.2: the domain is locally simplicial). So psi is continuous. H is continuous. If l* attains psi(s), then for any s' psi(s') <= the bracket at l* = psi(s) - sum of p_x <s'_x - s_x, l*_x>. QED.

(b) Let d = the largest over x, i of |log(s~_x[i] / s_x[i])| and eta = e^d - 1. Then, for every Z and k, L_Z(k)(s~) <= L + eta (L + sqrt(2 L)) + eta^2, with L = L_Z(k)(s). The same holds with s and s~ exchanged, and with d and eta unchanged. No C, K, k or tiny probability enters.
statements.proof: (a) KL(s~||q) = sum s~ log(s~/s) + sum s~ log(s/q), and sum s log(s/q) = KL(s||q). Subtract. (b) |s~_i - s_i| <= eta s_i, so |<s~ - s, log(s/q)>| <= eta E_s |log(s/q)|. With X = log(s/q): E_s |X| = E_s X + 2 E_s (-X)_+ = KL(s||q) + 2 E_s (log(q/s))_+ <= KL + 2 E_s (q/s - 1)_+ = KL + 2 TV <= KL + sqrt(2 KL), by log y <= y - 1 and Pinsker. KL(s~||s) <= log(1 + chi2(s~, s)) <= chi2 <= eta^2. Sum over x with weights p_x, and use Jensen on the square root. Take l along a minimising sequence for s. Each l of the class stays in the class, since the class does not depend on the table. QED. First-order tightness: I did not prove it. The true first-order change along a direction is the p-weighted mean of <s~ - s, log(s/q*)>. So the bound and the true worst slope are both of order E_s |log(s/q*)|, and E_s |X| <= L + sqrt(2L) is an inequality I have not matched from below in a centred form.
statements.covers: free codes, table, read (any fixed Z). A same-Z statement only: the box and a change of Z are not covered.
statements.check: 8 random tables (K = 8, C = 6, k = 2, perturbation of up to 0.05 in log ratio, largest difference after normalising). Fits stand in for L, so the bound is checked only on the samples. 0 fails, with bound around 1.2 to 1.3 times L~ (0.0747 to 0.0754, bound 0.0942). statements.slots: Slot 4, only in a limited form: it is a bound in one table error, 0 at error 0, size-free. It needs an error that counts every tail entry in log scale, and its first-order tightness is not proved. It gives a build no closed form on its own. It is the tool any table claim can use once an exact class exists.

statements.statement: F3 (the moment-curve build: rows with few moderate classes cost almost nothing at k = 2m - 1, for any number of classes). Let tau_i in [0, 1) be distinct with least gap gamma. Each row x has a set S_x of exactly m classes and tail mass zeta_x = s_x(off S_x) > 0. Let g_x be the polynomial of degree at most m - 1 with g_x(tau_i) = log s_x[i] on S_x, G = the largest of |g_x(tau_i)| over x and i, zeta = the least zeta_x, and lambda = (G + log(C / zeta)) gamma^(-2m). Then the logits l_x(i) = g_x(tau_i) - lambda p_x(tau_i), with p_x = the product over a in S_x of (tau - tau_a)^2, have rank at most 2m - 1 after one shared offset t_i = -lambda tau_i^(2m), modulo constants, and KL(s_x || softmax(l_x)) <= zeta_x (G + lambda) for each x. So L_table(2m - 1) <= the sum of p_x zeta_x (G + lambda). G <= m gamma^(-(m-1)) times the largest |log s_x[i]| on S_x. For m = 1: k = 1, G <= the largest |log s_x[top]|, and tails below C^(-2) give loss near 0. Any order of the classes works, and relatives need not be near each other.
statements.proof: p_x is monic of degree 2m. So p_x(tau) - tau^(2m) has degree at most 2m - 1, and g_x has degree at most m - 1 <= 2m - 1. The coefficient of tau^j, j = 1 to 2m - 1, is the code of unit j, with V's column j = tau^j. The constant term is a row constant. The top power, with one common lambda, is the offset t. On S_x: l_x = log s_x. Off S_x: p_x >= gamma^(2m), so l_x(i) <= G - lambda gamma^(2m) = -log(C / zeta) and e^(l_x(i)) <= zeta / C. So Z_x = s_x(S_x) + the sum of e^(l_x(i)) <= 1 - zeta_x + zeta <= 1, and log Z_x <= 0. KL = log Z_x + the sum off S_x of s_x[i] (log s_x[i] - l_x(i)), by direct substitution. Here log s_x[i] < 0, -g_x <= G and lambda p_x <= lambda, since |tau - tau_a| < 1. For G: |Lagrange basis| <= gamma^(-(m-1)) on [0, 1). QED.
statements.covers: free codes and table (explicit builds with free codes). Not the read or the box: no statement that z can compute these codes.
statements.check: Explicit builds at (C, m) = (12, 1), (40, 1), (12, 2), (30, 2), (30, 3). The numerical rank after the offset is exactly 2m - 1 each time. Max row KL is below the bound on four of the five. On (30, 3), zeta = 1e-30, the code counted 9 rows above the bound 9.9e-20, with max KL 2.2e-16. That is the rounding of log Z near 1, not a fail of the theorem, but this case is therefore not a check.
statements.slots: Fills no slot. It is an upper value at a tail near 0. It corrects a remark in DQ15's Route: a table near the identity needs only rank 1 with an offset (a parabola), not rank 2 on a circle. What it tells other tracks: at k >= 2m - 1, a slot 3 lower bound cannot read only each row's top m classes and their conditional odds. It must read how large the tail mass is against gamma^(2m), that is, about C^(-2m) for evenly spaced tau. Read as a network: this is the toy's world of the essay. Unrelated tops pack with almost no cost as long as the tail is thin enough.

statements.statement: F4 (a rank floor that charges for sharing, at a confident table with a graded tail). Let m classes and m rows have weights 1/m, s_j[j] = 1 - e, s_j[i] = e u_ji for i != j, with u_ji in [e^(-b), e^(b)] / (m - 1), the sum of u_ji over i equal to 1, and 0 < e < 1/4. Write M = log((1 - e)(m - 1) / e), n0 = 8k + 17, R = 0.47 M / sqrt(k + 2). Suppose m >= 3 n0, R >= b + 1 + log(32 n0 / 3) and M > 6. Then L_free(k) >= e Q0 for T empty, with Q0 = the least of: 3 (R - b - 1) e^(-b) / (128 n0); (M - 6) / 12; (1/e - 4) / 16. Leading term: about e M e^(-b) / (272 (k + 2)^(3/2)) for large k. Unequal weights: multiply by m times the least weight. On a larger table apply it to a minor of TQ22: a set of m classes, one row for each, with the row's conditional table on those classes meeting the premises.
statements.proof: Suppose L < e Q with Q = Q0. Take any build with loss below e Q (the least may be an infimum). Rank: B_ji = log q_j[i] - log(w_j / (m - 1)), with w_j = 1 - q_j[j], has rank at most k + 2 (t + V c has rank at most k + 1; the row constant adds 1). Step 1: at least 3m/4 rows have row loss Lambda_j <= 4 e Q (Markov); call them G. Step 2: for j in G the chain rule gives Lambda_j = kl(e || w_j) + e KL(u_j || q^_j), with q^_j the tail of q_j normalised. So KL(u_j || q^_j) <= 4 Q, and kl(e || w_j) <= 4 e Q. If w_j < e: kl(e||w) >= e log(e/w) - e, so log(e/w) <= 4Q + 1, and B_jj - M lies in [0, 4Q + 1 + log 2]. If w_j >= e, with y = w/e: kl >= e (y - 1 - log y) >= e (y/2 - log 2), so y <= 8Q + 2 and w <= 1/2 (from Q <= (1/e - 4)/16), so B_jj - M >= -log(8Q + 2) - log 2 >= -(4Q + 1 + log 2). So |B_jj - M| <= D := 4Q + 2, and M >= 3 D (from Q <= (M - 6)/12). Step 3 (outliers): off the diagonal B_ji = log((m - 1) q^_j[i]). Fewer than (m - 1) e^(-R) entries of a row have B_ji > R, since q^ sums to 1. For E = {i: B_ji < -R} with n elements: f = u_j(E) >= e^(-b) n / (m - 1), g = q^_j(E) <= e^(b - R) f. Data processing gives 4 Q >= kl(f || g) >= f log(f/g) - f + g >= f (R - b - 1). So n <= (m - 1) e^b 4 Q / (R - b - 1). So each row in G has at most gamma (m - 1) outliers, with gamma = 4 Q e^b / (R - b - 1) + e^(-R) <= 3/(32 n0) + 3/(32 n0) = 3/(16 n0). Step 4 (Turan): the outlier graph on G has at most |G| gamma (m - 1) edges, so it has an independent set of size at least |G| / (1 + 2 gamma (m - 1)). This is at least n0 in both cases: at least 3/(16 gamma) >= n0 if 2 gamma (m - 1) >= 1, otherwise at least 3m/8 >= n0. Step 5 (trace): on such a set T of n0 rows and classes, B restricted has rank at most k + 2, with diagonal in M +- D and off-diagonal entries of size at most R. So tr <= sqrt(rank) |.|_F gives n0 (M - D)^2 <= (k + 2)((M + D)^2 + n0 R^2). M >= 3D gives (M - D) >= 2M/3 and (M + D)/(M - D) <= 2, and R^2 <= (M - D)^2 / (2 (k + 2)) (0.47 <= (2/3)/sqrt 2). So n0 (M - D)^2 / 2 <= (k + 2)(M + D)^2, so n0 <= 8 (k + 2) = 8k + 16 < n0. Contradiction. QED.
statements.covers: free codes and table with T empty. Through TQ11 part 2 it is a floor for every network with k new top units and no kept units, so the read and the box as well. Not for kept units.
statements.check: The floor is 0 on every size I can fit (it needs M >= 24 at k = 1, 29 at k = 2, 70 at k = 14). Fits on the symmetric table at k = 2, e = 0.05: m = 16, 64, 256 give 0.52, 1.52, 2.76 nats, which is growth of about 0.9 log m, so the theorem's shape is right but it is far from tight. These fits are upper values and they check nothing below the floor.
statements.slots: No slot: it is a lower bound with no matching build. It is new against TQ22: it reads classes across families, and it counts k. On a real table the premise fails: with conditional tail mass e near 0.01 and m near 100, M is about 9, against 70 at k = 14. So it has no value at ResNet numbers. Expected, not proved: the true least on this table at fixed k grows like log m, and a sharp form would use a better step than the trace.

statements.statement: F5 (a table-distance error cannot give a size-free bound). For every k >= 1, every e in (0, 1/8] and every b >= 0, and every size-free function f with f(x) -> 0 as x -> 0, the promise |L_table(k)(s) - L_table(k)(s')| <= f(max row distance in L1) fails. Precisely: there are tables s0 and s_e on the same m classes, each confident in its top class on every row, with the same graded tail shape u_ji in [e^(-b), e^(b)] / (m - 1), tail masses zeta and e, and row distance 2(e - zeta) in L1, such that L_table(k)(s0) -> 0 and L_table(k)(s_e) >= (1 - 4e)/16 - o(1) as m grows. Consequence for a claim type: suppose a claim type has error E with |E(s) - E(s')| <= w(|s - s'|_1), w size-free and w(x) -> 0, and suppose a closed form at error 0 and a bound f(E). If some claim at s0 has error near 0 and closed form near 0, the bound fails at s_e for small e. So a slot 4 error cannot be size-free in table distance. It must see tail entries in log scale, as F2's does.
statements.proof: s0: F3 with m = 1, zeta = m^(-4), gamma = 1/m: L_table(1)(s0) <= zeta (G + log(m/zeta) m^2), with G = -log(1 - zeta), which tends to 0. L_table(k) is non-increasing in k. s_e: F4, where as m grows R and M tend to infinity, so the least of the three terms is (1/e - 4)/16 once m is large enough, which gives L >= e (1/e - 4)/16 = (1 - 4e)/16. Both tables have constancy claims at error 0 and, for a tree-shaped u, LCA-level claims at error 0. QED. Read as a network: two networks have the same top class on every photo and the same relatives order. One has almost all of its mass on the top class and the other leaves 5% in the tail. The first can be written by one unit, and the second cannot be written by k units at any fixed k. So the tail mass, the dark knowledge, is what a small network pays for. Said plainly about size: the theorem needs m near exp(c (k + 2)^(3/2) / e), far beyond any real network. Fits show the same effect at small m (0.52 nats at m = 16, k = 2, e = 0.05), but that is not proved.
statements.covers: table and free codes with T empty; through TQ11 part 2 the lower side also holds for read and box. The s0 side is a free-code build only.
statements.check: Fits at k = 2: e near 0 gives 0.0000 at m = 16, 64, 256, and e = 0.05 gives 0.52, 1.52, 2.76, at row distance 0.1. Upper values only.
statements.slots: A conditional impossibility for slot 4, for one class of error (uniformly continuous in table distance). Slot 4 as a whole stays open, since F2 is a size-free bound in a stronger error. The instance is confident, relatives may be likelier than strangers, and the constancy and LCA-level claims hold at error 0. It is not a claim that real tables look like s0.

statements.statement: F6 (crossing rows; the exact threshold on the size of a row's top set). Let classes have points b_i in R^k and offsets t_i, with logits l_y(i) = t_i + b_i . c_y. (a) Crossing lemma. Let S, S' be disjoint class sets with conv(b_S) and conv(b_S') meeting. Then, for rows x with set S and y with set S', either some i in S' has l_x(i) >= min over S of l_x, or some i in S has l_y(i) >= min over S' of l_y. Call a row bad if a class outside its set reaches its set's least logit. (b) Payment. A bad row with sigma = the least s on its set, varsigma = the largest s off its set, sigma >= varsigma, pays KL >= Pay(sigma, varsigma) = (sigma + varsigma)(log 2 - h(varsigma / (sigma + varsigma))), h the binary entropy. For varsigma -> 0 this is sigma log 2. (c) Threshold. Let U be 2m + 3 classes, and let the table hold a row with set S for every (m + 1)-subset S of U. Then, at any tail depth, L_table(2m) >= the least over those rows of p_x Pay(sigma_x, varsigma_x). While at k = 2m + 1, F3 gives L_table(2m + 1) -> 0 as the tails go to 0, with the moderate entries fixed. So the least rank for all (m + 1)-sets is exactly 2m + 1, for rows of any confidence on their set. (d) m = 1. If rows are the edges E of a graph G on C classes, at k = 2 the good rows form a planar graph, so at least E - mp(G) rows are bad, with mp(G) the largest planar subgraph, and mp(G) <= 3C - 6: L_table(2) >= (least p_x Pay) (E - mp(G)). If G is planar, L_table(2) -> 0 as the tail goes to 0.
statements.proof: (a) Let p be in both hulls, p = sum alpha_i b_i = sum alpha'_j b_j, h = sum alpha_i t_i, h' = sum alpha'_j t_j. If h >= h': sum alpha_i l_y(i) = h + p . c_y >= h' + p . c_y = sum alpha'_j l_y(j) >= min over S' of l_y, so some i in S has l_y(i) >= min over S' of l_y. If h <= h', the same holds for row x. (b) Let j be the class of least logit on the set, and i the class reaching it, so q[j] <= q[i]. Chain rule on {j, i} against the rest: KL >= (s[j] + s[i]) kl(s[j] / (s[j] + s[i]) || q[j] / (q[j] + q[i])). The second argument is at most 1/2, and the first is at least 1/2, so kl >= kl(first || 1/2) = log 2 - h(s[i] / (s[j] + s[i])). The function is increasing in s[j] and decreasing in s[i] when s[j] >= s[i], by direct derivative: log(2 s[j] / (s[j] + s[i])) >= 0 and log(2 s[i] / (s[j] + s[i])) <= 0. (c) Van Kampen-Flores: any map of the m-skeleton of the (2m + 2)-simplex into R^(2m) has two disjoint faces with meeting images. Apply it to the affine map i -> b_i with k <= 2m (embed R^k in R^(2m)). (a) gives a bad row, and (b) gives its payment. L_table is non-increasing in k. The k = 2m + 1 side is F3 with m + 1 in place of m. (d) Good rows' edges: two with disjoint endpoints have disjoint closed segments, by (a). Disjoint compact segments stay disjoint under a small move of the points. A generic small move then makes adjacent edges meet only at the shared endpoint. So the good graph is planar, with a straight-line embedding. For planar G: extend to a triangulation. Steinitz gives a 3-polytope, and a projective map gives a concave lift (b_i, t_i) over a polygon in which each edge has a functional (c, 1) that ties on it and is strictly below elsewhere. Scale by lambda, and tilt c by a fixed small vector for the odds. With lambda -> infinity and zeta lambda -> 0 the loss tends to 0. This last clause is a limit, and it has no size bound here. QED.
statements.covers: free codes and table with T empty; the floor in (c) and (d) also holds for read and box through TQ11 part 2, and for any network with k new top units. Tiny entries are not divided by: the floor needs sigma_x p_x only. Sources to enter the literature table: van Kampen 1932, Flores 1933, Steinitz.
statements.check: Fits at tail 1e-6 or 1e-7. k = 2: K5 0.0723 against floor 0.0347; K33 0.0792 against 0.0385; K6 0.172 against 0.0693 (Euler count); K5 minus one edge 7e-5; octahedron 8e-5. 7 classes at m = 2: all triples at k = 4: 0.0183 against 0.0066; all triples at k = 5 and k = 6: 0.00000; all pairs at k = 4: 0.00000. These are upper values, and they never fall below the floor.
statements.slots: No slot: no matching least at a loss above 0. It is a lower bound with no tiny number, with no span and with no projector, and it reads which sets are on a row, not how each row is tilted. It gives other tracks the exact line: k >= 2m + 1 when every top set of size m + 1 occurs. Limit on reach: with 1000 classes and few rows the count E - mp(G) can be 0, and at k = 14 the threshold needs all sets of size 8 inside 17 classes, which real rows do not supply. It is the top-sets part of the cost only.

statements.statement: F7 (attempt at NP-hardness of slot 3 at k = 1, and the exact step where it stops). Let rows be the edges of a graph G on C classes, uniform on the pair with tail zeta. Call a row good when |l(a) - l(b)| <= M0/2 and every other class is at least M0 below min(l(a), l(b)). Proved: at k = 1 the good rows form a linear forest, for any M0 > 0. So at most lf(G) rows are good, with lf(G) the largest linear forest in G, and lf(G) = C - 1 exactly when G has a Hamiltonian path. A row that is not good pays at least pay1 = the least of (1 - zeta) log cosh(M0/4) and (sigma + varsigma) kl(sigma / (sigma + varsigma) || 1 / (1 + e^(-M0))), about 0.083 nats at M0 = 1.7. So L_table(1) >= (least p_x) pay1 (E - lf(G)), a floor in an NP-hard quantity. Not proved: NP-hardness of L_table(1). The step that stops it: the upper side. A row that is not good has no fixed price: its price grows with the distance of its two classes along the line, so a threshold test cannot separate a yes instance from a no instance.
statements.proof: Linear forest. Shift so that x_a = 0, t_a = 0. Let b, c lie on one side of a, with rho = x_b / x_c > 0. Let r_b = l(a) - l(b) in row (a, b), and r_c = l(a) - l(c) in row (a, c), both of size at most M0/2. Row (a, c) gives t_b - rho (r_c + t_c) <= -r_c - M0. Row (a, b) gives t_c - (r_b + t_b) / rho <= -r_b - M0. Multiply the second by rho and add: (1 - rho)(r_c - r_b) <= -M0 (1 + rho). The left side is at least -|1 - rho| M0, and this is strictly above -M0 (1 + rho). Contradiction. So each class has at most one good neighbour on each side. If b sits on a's point: l(b) = t_b in every row, and |t_b| <= M0/2 from row (a, b), while row (a, c), c != b, needs t_b <= -M0: contradiction, so a has only that neighbour. A graph with at most one neighbour on each side of a line has no cycle, so it is a linear forest. Payment: odds off by more than M0/2 cost at least (1 - zeta) kl(1/2 || 1 / (1 + e^(M0/2))) = (1 - zeta) log cosh(M0/4). A class within M0 of the set's least gives the second term, by the chain rule on the pair, as in F6(b). Hamiltonian path in G is NP-complete, and lf(G) = C - 1 exactly then. Where it stops, with numbers: fits at k = 1, tail 1e-7: path P5 0.00000; cycle C5 0.416 (one bad row pays about 2.08, against the floor pay1 of 0.083, 25 times more); Petersen 0.882. A yes instance with extra edges keeps bad rows, and each one costs up to about sigma times the logit range of the line. A no instance has one more bad row at no more than the floor. So the two values overlap unless the extra-edge count is 0, and then G is itself a linear forest and the question is trivial. Also proved as a limit of the method: a zero-bad reduction at k = 1 is a consecutive-ones test, and at k = 2 for pair rows a planarity test. Both are polynomial. So a zero-bad reduction must start at k >= 3 or use sets larger than pairs. A cap on the price does not exist: s[b] log(s[b]/q[b]) grows with log(1/q[b]), with no ceiling. A chain must have range at least about M0 j at distance j. The problem of bounded distance at k = 1 is of bandwidth type and is polynomial at fixed bandwidth (Saxe), which is why I did not expect a cap to rescue it.
statements.covers: table with T empty, k = 1 and, for the planar form, k = 2.
statements.check: The fits above, upper values only. star K1,3 0.0878 and the subdivided star 0.1618 lie above their floors (0.028 and 0.014 at pay1 = 0.083).
statements.slots: Fills no slot. What a successful hardness proof must use: (1) a yes instance with zero or uniformly priced bad rows; (2) a floor for bad rows that does not depend on the distance; (3) a gadget where a bad row's cost is exact, not only bounded below.

statements.statement: F7b (why Gillis-Glineur and Peeters do not transplant, as a statement). At second order, the weights of Lemma TQ20's Newton fit are W_xi = q_x[i], and the target is built on the same q_x. So the weight pattern is not free: log W, row-centred, has rank at most k + 1. A binary weight pattern with rows S_x is available at small loss only if the S_x are faces in the sense of F6(a) (a row's set has no outside class reaching its least). At the same time, if |S_x| <= (k + 1)/2 for all x, F3 says that the rows' moderate entries can be written exactly, so there is no fitting problem left. So a reduction that keeps a hard weighted low-rank problem must use rows with |S_x| > (k + 1)/2, with S_x realised as faces in dimension k, with margins polynomial in bits.
statements.proof: The first claim is the form of softmax: log q_x = l_x - log Z_x, with l_x in the class. The second is F6(a,b): a set with an outside class at or above its least pays Pay(sigma, varsigma), so at loss far below that payment it is a face. The third is F3. DQ4's gaps: (ii) and (iii) can be closed only when a realisation has small entries and the no case has a local proof. F6 and F7 give such a local proof for the lower side. Gap (i) (metric per row, rank tied to q) is what this statement sharpens, and it stays open. (iv) is not reached. So DQ4's route is not closed. Peeters' free entries (at the edges) have no counterpart here: every entry of a row is either near the set level or below it, so the pattern has no free entry. Bhangale-Kopparty goes through stretchability, whose realisations need coordinates doubly exponential in size, and a table would then need exponentially many bits for the margins.
statements.covers: table with T empty
statements.check: none beyond those of F3 and F6
statements.slots: No slot. It is the requirement list for a reduction: rows larger than (k + 1)/2, faces, and a local proof in the no case. Hardness remains neither proved nor refuted.

statements.statement: F8 (a jump for the read, with no kept units, beyond TQ17.1's instance). Let the group S hold two units on P with z_u = f and z_v = f + e g, e > 0, with f, g on P and 1, f, g independent, and let the out-weights of v be 0, so N is the same for every e. Then the share of z_v's variance outside the span of 1 and z_u tends to 0 with e, and for every e > 0 the one-read code class Z is the span of 1, f, g, whatever e is. So L_on(k) and V_b(k) do not depend on e > 0. If L_on with Z = span(1, f) at e = 0 is above L_(span(1, f, g))(k), the least jumps as e -> 0+, by an amount that does not depend on e. So an error that treats nearly parallel units of a group as parallel cannot carry a graded bound for the read or the box.
statements.proof: The span of 1, f, f + e g is the span of 1, f, g for each e != 0. So Definition DQ9's class is the same, with read weights of size 1/e. At e = 0 it is a smaller class. Strictness is possible: take k = 1, a table with three constant rows on C = 4 classes in general position, and g equal to a function of region: with free codes the least is that of two independent code values, whereas with span(1, f) the code is constrained. Any L_Z is non-increasing in Z. For V_b: a unit stays on with beta large, so V_b(k) <= L_on(k) at e > 0, and for e = 0 V_b is bounded below by the free least on the code class of relu of affine in f, which is a smaller class of functions of f alone. QED. Limit on the claim: the last step gives a jump for V_b only where every code that is a function of f alone is worse than the read through f and g. That holds, for example, when f is constant on P (then every unit is constant at e = 0), and it is only for such instances that I claim it. Read as a network: a unit that is almost a copy of another, with a small extra part, is a source of a read direction when the weights are free. Weight decay is what limits this in training, and the owner removed the cap, so the objective does not limit it.

result.summary: I have a proved lower bound on the floor L_free(k) with no span pinning and no 1/(smallest probability), read from N's own log table, plus an exact statement that TQ22 is sharp for every family of minors, so any charge for sharing units must read the entries between families. statements.statement: B1 (entry form, a Poisson association model). Let psi(y) = e^y - 1 - y, n_xi = p_x s_x[i], T_xi = log s_x[i]. For any logits l on a row, KL(s || softmax l) = min over a of the sum over i of s_i psi(l_i - a - T_i), attained at a = log sum e^(l_i). So L_free(k) = min over rank-limited L and row offsets a of the sum over x, i of n_xi psi(L_xi - a_x - T_xi). This is a rank-k log-bilinear (Goodman RC(k), from memory) fit of the joint table n. At k = 0 with free offset it is the mutual information of row and class. At the a above, e_i = l_i - a - T_i = log(q_i / s_i).
statements.proof: The sum equals e^(-a) sum e^(l_i) - 1 - <s, l> + a + <s, T>. It is convex in a, with minimum at e^a = sum e^(l_i). The value is log sum e^(l_i) - <s, l> - H(s) = KL(s || softmax l). QED.

statements.statement: B2 (row lemma in the row's own metric). Let s > 0 on C classes, T = log s, theta > 0, w_i = s_i min(1, s_i / theta). Let S be a subspace of R^C with 1 in S, and A^2 = min over h in S of the sum of w_i (h_i - T_i)^2. For beta > 0 let R(beta) = max over 0 < tau <= 1/beta of tau - (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta). Explicitly R(beta) = 1/beta - 1/beta^2 for beta >= 5/2, and otherwise the value at tau = (sqrt(1 + 6 beta) - 1) / (3 beta). R tends to 1/2 as beta -> 0, and R is decreasing. Then for every l in S: KL(s || softmax l) >= A^2 R(A / sqrt(theta)).
statements.proof: Let h be the minimiser and e = h - T. The normal equations say the sum of w_i e_i f_i = 0 for f in S. Let t_i = min(1, s_i / theta) and v_i = tau t_i e_i, so s_i v_i = tau w_i e_i. Then E_s[v f] = 0 for f in S; f = 1 gives E_s v = 0. Since w_i e_i^2 <= A^2 and t_i / sqrt(w_i) = sqrt(t_i / s_i) <= 1 / sqrt(theta), we get tau t_i (e_i)_- <= tau A / sqrt(theta) = tau beta <= 1, so q° = s(1 + v) is a distribution. Donsker-Varadhan: KL(s || softmax l) = log E_s e^(l - T) - E_s(l - T) >= E_s[v (l - T)] - KL(q° || s). Gain: for l in S, E_s[v (l - T)] = tau sum w_i e_i (l_i - T_i) = tau sum w_i e_i (h_i - T_i) = tau A^2. Cost: KL(q° || s) = E_s phi(v), phi(v) = (1+v) log(1+v) - v. We have phi(v) <= v^2 / 2 for v >= 0, and for v = -r, r in [0, 1], phi = sum over n >= 2 of r^n / (n(n-1)) <= r^2/2 + r^3/2. So cost <= (1 + tau beta)/2 times the sum of s_i v_i^2 <= (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta) sum w_i e_i^2 (t_i <= 1). Net tau A^2 - (tau^2 A^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta). Take the best tau. QED. The first-order terms cancel exactly, by the normal equations: basing the dual point at s in the row's metric leaves no defect in the linear term. The only price is the cap v >= -1.

statements.statement: B3 (spectral lower bound on the floor, in product scalings; nested layers allowed) (under: none). Let layers l = 1, ..., M have row sets R_l, class sets H_l, a^l > 0 on R_l, b^l > 0 on H_l with sum 1, and for each entry the sum over l of a^l_x b^l_i <= n_xi. Let That^l be T on R_l x H_l, double-centred: subtract each row's b-mean, then each class's a-weighted mean. Let r^l_x = the L2(b^l) norm of row x of That^l, and beta = max over x, i of (sum over l of a^l_x sqrt(b^l_i) r^l_x) / n_xi. Then L_free(k) >= R(beta) times the sum over l, over j > k, of sigma_j^2(D_(a^l)^(1/2) That^l D_(b^l)^(1/2)). No span is pinned. The bound reads only s and p. With r kept directions, replace k by k + r. Since L_Z >= L_free and V_b(k) >= L_free(k) by TQ11 part 1, it holds for the read and the box as a floor. Scale fact: if all a^l are multiplied by alpha, the sigma^2 and beta both scale with alpha. For large beta, R(beta) ~ 1/beta, so a common tail scale cancels in the ratio.
statements.proof: Fix a competitor (t, V, c). For layer l let Pi_l be the L2(b^l)-orthogonal projector on R^(H_l) onto the complement of the span of 1 and V restricted to H_l (dimension at most k + 1). Let g^l_x = Pi_l That^l_x. For tau <= 1/beta let delta_xi = -(tau / p_x) sum over l of a^l_x b^l_i g^l_xi, and q°_x = s_x + delta_x. Row sums: <g, 1>_b = 0. Moment: V^T delta_x = 0. Offset: the sum over x of p_x <delta_x, t> is -tau sum over l of <Pi_l (sum over x of a_x That_x), t>_b = 0, by the column centring. Positivity: |g_xi| <= |g_x|_b / sqrt(b_i) <= r_x / sqrt(b_i), so |delta_xi| / s_xi <= tau beta <= 1. Donsker-Varadhan on each row: D >= sum p_x <delta_x, l_x - T_x> - sum p_x KL(q°_x || s_x). The l part vanishes. The -T part: T_x on H_l is That_x plus a row constant plus a vector free of x, and both extras integrate to 0, so it equals tau E with E = sum over l, x of a_x |g_x|_b^2. Cost: as in B2, at most ((1 + tau beta)/2) sum over x, i of (p_x delta_xi)^2 / n_xi; by Cauchy (sum a b g)^2 <= (sum a b)(sum a b g^2) <= n_xi sum a b g^2, so cost <= (tau^2 / 2)(1 + tau beta) E. So D >= R(beta) E. Eckart-Young for each layer: with M = D_a^(1/2) That D_b^(1/2), M sqrt(b) = 0, and in scaled coordinates Pi_l removes sqrt(b) and at most k further directions, so a_x-sum of |g_x|_b^2 = |M Pi~|_F^2 >= sum over j > k of sigma_j^2(M). QED.

statements.statement: B4 (scaled certificate; TQ18 part 1 is the case a b^T = constant) (under: none). Let (t, V, c) be a stationary rank-k triple for free codes, with Y = R 1, q = softmax(t + V c), m = p q, G = D_p (s - q). Let a, b > 0, kappa = max a_x b_i / m_xi. Gauge: Vtilde = D_b^(1/2) V orthonormal and orthogonal to sqrt(b); ctilde = D_a^(1/2) c orthogonal to sqrt(a). Let Gtilde = D_a^(-1/2) G D_b^(-1/2), g = |Gtilde|_op, sigma = the least singular value of ctilde, Btilde = ctilde (ctilde^T ctilde)^(-1), w = 2 kappa g^2, R = Gtilde + w Btilde Vtilde^T. If (i) 2 kappa g <= sigma and (ii) sqrt(a_x b_i) |R_x|_2 <= m_xi for all x, i, then L_free(k) = D(t, V, c). Necessity of (ii) for this form: for each x, i and any 1 <= k, some competitor span gives (R E)_xi = (1/2)(|r_x| |e_i| + r_x[i]) - Gtilde_xi, with r_x and e_i the parts of R_x and e_i orthogonal to sqrt(b); so a dual point linear in one projector, in any class and row scaling, needs (ii) up to a factor about 2.
statements.proof: Competitor (t', V', c'). Choose a dimension k+1 subspace holding sqrt(b) and D_b^(1/2) V', and let Pi' be the projector onto its complement. Pi_0 is the same for Vtilde, and E = Pi' - Pi_0, so |E|_op <= 1, |E|_F^2 = 2 X, X = tr(Vtilde^T Pi' Vtilde). Stationarity gives Gtilde sqrt(b) = 0, Gtilde Vtilde = 0, ctilde^T Gtilde = 0, sqrt(a)^T Gtilde = 0, and R Pi_0 = Gtilde. Also |R|_op = max(g, w / sigma) = g under (i). Let G° = D_a^(1/2) R Pi' D_b^(1/2), q°_x = s_x - G°_x / p_x = q_x - d_x, with d_xi = sqrt(a_x b_i) (R E)_xi / p_x. Rows sum to 0; G° V' = 0; 1^T G° = 0 as sqrt(a)^T R = 0. So the sum of p_x <q° - s, l'> = 0 and D(l') >= sum p_x (H(q°_x) - H(s_x)). (ii) gives d_xi <= q_xi. Expanding H by (E) of TQ17: the linear term, with the parts in 1, log Z and t vanishing, is tr(ctilde^T R E Vtilde) = w X. Remainder: m phi(-d/q) <= p^2 d^2 / m = (a b / m)(R E)^2, total <= kappa g^2 2 X. Net (w - 2 kappa g^2) X = 0. And D(t, V, c) = sum p_x (H(q_x) - H(s_x)) at a stationary triple. Necessity: over unit vectors u in the span of r and e, the maximum of (r.u)(u.e) is (|r||e| + r.e)/2. Take Pi' = u u^T + a projector orthogonal to u, r, e, sqrt(b). QED.

Tildes are scaling by D_a^(1/2), D_b^(1/2), and Y~ = D_a^(-1/2) Y D_b^(-1/2). (1) For any Y supported on W1: LRA_d >= 2 <Y, T> - sum Y^2 / W1 + mu |T~|_F^2 - (1/mu) (sum over j <= d of sigma_j^2(mu T~ + Y~)). This is concave in Y. (2) If L = c V^T has rank d and is stationary, with G = W o (T - L), G V = 0, c^T G = 0, and |G~|_op <= mu sigma_d(L~), then L is the global least and (1) holds with equality at Y = W1 o (T - L). (3) The price of sharing. On N directions split into J blocks, T~ = tau I, W = theta on diagonal blocks and mu off them: LRA_d >= N theta mu tau^2 (N - d) / (d theta + mu (N - d)), with equality when a rank-d projector has every diagonal block equal to (d/N) I. With eps = mu / theta, the share of the energy lost is eps (N - d) / (d + eps (N - d)): it tends to 0 as eps -> 0 (free gluing), it equals 1 - d/N at eps = 1 (Eckart-Young), and it turns over at eps (N/d - 1) about 1.

(2) f(L') - f(L) = |L' - L|_W^2 - 2 <G, L'> >= mu |L~' - L~|^2 - 2 <G~, L~'> = mu (|L~' - Z|^2 - |G~ / mu|^2), with Z = L~ + G~ / mu. G~ and L~ are orthogonal on both sides, so the singular values of Z are those of L~ and of G~ / mu. Under the test the top d are L~'s, so the Eckart-Young floor of |L~' - Z|^2 is |G~ / mu|^2. statements.statement: B6 (TQ22 is sharp for every family of minors; sharing can cost nothing) (under: none). Given any J minors, each with rows R_b, classes H_b (the R_b disjoint, the H_b disjoint), weights pi_x > 0 and positive conditional tables s^b on H_b, there is a table on the classes of the H_b with exactly these minors, for which L_free(k) = the sum over b of L^(b)(k). Construction: take minimisers (t_b, V_b, c_b) of the minors, stack them into (t, V, c), let q_x = softmax(t + V c_x); for x in R_b put s_x = q_x off H_b, s_x = q_x(H_b) s^b_x on H_b, and p_x = pi_x / q_x(H_b). So no bound that reads only the minors can charge for sharing units. Any charge must read the entries between families.
statements.proof: Minimisers exist: s^b > 0 makes each minor coercive modulo constants, and rank <= k is closed. The new table's minor b has conditional s^b and weight p_x s_x(H_b) = pi_x. Lower side: TQ22. Upper side: chain rule over the partition of the classes into H_b and singletons: KL(s_x || q_x) = s_x(H_b) KL(s^b_x || q_x | H_b), as the part-level masses agree. q_x | H_b = softmax of the minor's own logits, because V restricted to H_b is V_b and c_x = c_b row x. Sum: the sum of the minors' leasts. QED.

statements.statement: B7 (pole minors on shared units: exact at k = C/(2J), and what it costs). Let k >= 2, J >= 1, C = 2kJ, families H_b of 2k classes, rows = classes, invertible k x k matrices G_b. Let V on H_b have rows G_b^T (+/- e_j) on the two classes of pair j; the code of a class with sign sigma on pair j be tau sigma G_b^(-1) e_j; t any vector; q = softmax(t + V c). Let pi_c = p_c q_c(H_b) and let (pi, t on H_b, tau, mu_b) be in the pole family of DQ13. On H_b put s_c = q_c(H_b) (q_c | H_b + (mu_b / pi_c) Pi* e_c); off H_b put s_c = q_c. Then L_free(k) = the sum over b of the TQ17 closed form. If G_b G_b'^(-1) has all entries of size 1/sqrt(k) (mutually unbiased bases; real sets of size k/2 + 1 at k = 4^m, from memory), the off-family logits are +/- tau / sqrt(k) around t, so the top class is confident for large tau. C reaches k (k + 2), so k is near sqrt(C). Limit, proved: with t constant on each family and J >= 2, no such table has every in-family tail class at or above every off-family class on every row. So this family holds relatives no likelier than strangers: it is the toy's world, and the essay's line 701 says this is where packing is right.
statements.proof: Exactness: B6 with TQ17 for each minor. The conditional on H_b is softmax(t on H_b + tau (e_c - e_c')) since V on H_b applied to the code gives tau (e_c - e_c'), and K = 2k. Limit: M = G_b' G_b^(-1) is invertible. Take a nonzero entry M_(j'j) of size x > 0 and signs so that row a of family b has logit t_b' + tau x on a class of family b'. Likewise a nonzero entry of M^(-1) of size y > 0 gives a row of family b' with logit t_b + tau y on a class of family b. Being below the tail level on both rows needs t_b >= t_b' + tau x and t_b' >= t_b + tau y, so tau (x + y) <= 0, false. A flat gate unit would repair this, but then V on H_b has rank k - 1 modulo constants, while TQ22 still gives the minor k units, so the bound falls strictly below the fit unless L^(b)(k) = L^(b)(k-1). QED.

statements.statement: B8 (product form is self-defeating as a claim). If on R x H the conditional rows satisfy |log(s_x|H / b)| <= B for one distribution b, then the minor's least at every k >= 0 is at most the sum over R of p_x s_x(H) (e^B - 1)^2. So a claim 'the weights are product form on this block', with error B, has at error 0 a block with loss 0. Answer to the track's question: no real structure gives exact product form in the table's metric within a family with a loss above 0 there. Product form in the fit's metric would need units flat on the family, which TQ21 part 5 and LADDER 47 show loses at confidence. At confidence the part of the table close to a product is the stranger block, not the family: envelope a b^T / W has minimum 0.000 and median 0.36 at top 0.91.
statements.proof: Take the offset log b and code 0: KL(s|H || b) <= chi^2(s|H || b) <= max (s|H / b - 1)^2 <= (e^B - 1)^2. Multiply by the row weight and sum. QED.

statements.statement: Measured failure on one synthetic table (F=4 families, S=3, M=4, C=48, level strengths g = (1.5, 2, 4), noise 0.4, top 0.91; family mass 0.981). It is not a theorem and not an impossibility on a trained-like instance. The premise of this track, that at second order TQ20 is weighted low-rank fitting and this holds where the loss is, is false on the entries that carry the loss. At a fit, the share of the KL on entries with |log(q/s)| > 1 is 0.86, 0.95, 0.85, 0.65, 0.51 at k = 2, 5, 11, 24, 36. The share on entries with e < -1 is 0.53, 0.77, 0.76, 0.64, 0.51, on mass of only 0.031 down to below 0.001. By kind, strangers pushed down hold 45%, 60%, 70%, 81% at k = 2, 5, 11, 24; own class falls from 14% to 0. The largest |e| is 95.6, 18.5, 8.7, 7.5. On mass >= 0.01 the largest downward e is only 0.19, 0.08, 0.02 at k = 5, 11, 24, so the top classes are in the quadratic regime and the tails are not.
statements.proof: Why it fails. psi(e) is about |e| for e far below 0, so the entries pay linearly. The quadratic value (1/2) n e^2 overstates them by 17, 4.2, 2.4, 2.5, 2.4 times. The least of (1/2) n (T - L)^2 is 0.557, 0.137, 0.030, 0.0034 at rank k = 2, 5, 11, 24 against L = 0.80, 0.116, 0.0186, 0.0019: the same order, but neither a bound nor close, and on the wrong side at k >= 5. Every proof of mine turns the quadratic into a KL bound through the cap v >= -1, and that costs R(beta) with beta of 5 to 6 at the best layers. Tail minors, fitted, hold 0.1% of L, so conditioning on far families does not find this loss either: it is interference written by units in use elsewhere, seen as noise on strangers. This fits the essay's phrase that the toy prices interference; B5 part 3 prices it, but only at second order.

statements.statement: Attempts that failed, each with the step. (a) Huber low rank: psi >= a Huber function with no tiny number, by direct entrywise bounds, but Eckart-Young has no Huber form. (b) One-sided row metric: a dual with v >= 0 on tail classes needs no theta, but the resulting one-sided problem has competitors going far below at no cost in the bound, so rank is not seen (gates are free). (c) A sup-norm bound through leverage (Lunin, Lewis weights): the restricted form with a constant depending only on span dimension and removed mass is false. Counterexample: f^2 = 2^(-j) on L equal-mass levels has sup / mean = L/2 on every set of mass at least 1 - delta, up to (1 - delta). (d) Row-outlier bootstrap: min(A_x^2, u) with interlacing needs too many removed rows. At n = 48 it removes about 14 and leaves rank 40 of 48; on photos it is worse. (e) Forster sign rank: identity-like sign patterns have rank 2, as the circle fact says; family patterns have a large top singular value, so the bound is about 1.

result.blocked_by: Eckart-Young needs a quadratic in the competitor's logit error, but psi(e) has no global quadratic lower bound: for e far below 0, psi grows like |e|. Any step from KL to a rank bound therefore needs a sup-norm cap on a residual that depends on the competitor's span. That cap costs the factor R(beta). On a confident table most of the loss sits on entries with e < -1, so the capped metric w_xi <= s_xi min(1, s_xi / theta) discards the regime that holds the loss. The missing statement is a lower bound for rank-limited weighted L1 fitting of the log table on stranger blocks, in the form: for every rank-k L, the sum of n_xi |L_xi - a_x - T_xi| is at least a number computable from T, with no 1 / (smallest probability).
result.next: What I would try next: a first-order charge on stranger blocks, where the weights are close to product form (B8), for a sum of n_xi |e_xi| over rank-limited L. I have no tool for weighted L1 low rank; a dual with bounded entries needs a bound on entries of a projected table, which is the same sup-norm problem. I would also try B5 part 3 with L1 cost in place of squared cost on the off-family blocks, to get a price of sharing valid for KL. What other tracks could give: (1) an exact family with relatives above strangers, since B7 proves pole minors cannot supply one, and a flat gate breaks the minors bound; a bound that charges a flat unit (a quotient of TQ22, with k - 1 units on the family when a gate is forced) is the concrete object. (2) Delsarte-type bounds for the exponential barrier at universally optimal codes, for the symmetric clean check. (3) A measurement next round, cheap and from N alone: on ResNet tables, the B3 reach, the share of KL with |e| > 1, and the B5 test ratio in the s-metric envelope. These decide whether the synthetic failure carries over, and I have not run them. result.summary: On four classes and two units, I proved the exact least for a table with two related families, at any top-class confidence, and the units are a family unit plus one unit shared across families, with relatives on one pole. The cost of that shared unit is the mutual information between family and position in each row, and it is 0 exactly when the within-family contrasts agree across families, but graded weights can beat it, and a table with 4 classes fills no slot. For J families or larger families I have only an upper bound and a sandwich, and I proved that no dual point with fixed rows can go much further on tables with tiny tails.

statements.statement: Lemma A1 (one missing direction). Let C = k + 2, with any rows, weights p_x and positive s_x. For a unit vector n orthogonal to 1, let Phi(n) = sup over (a_x) with sum p_x a_x = 0 and s_x + a_x n >= 0 of sum p_x [H(s_x + a_x n) - H(s_x)]. Then L_free(k) = min over n of Phi(n). Phi(n) is the exact least over logits with <n, l_x> = tau for one tau.
statements.proof: Any V has rank at most k, so span(1, V) has dimension at most C - 1. So some unit n is orthogonal to 1 and to V. The logits then meet <n, l_x> = <n, t> = tau. Conversely, any logits with <n, l_x> = tau have the form t + V c_x, with V a basis of the complement of (1, n). Weak side: with A the log-sum-exp, KL(s || softmax(l)) = A(l) - <s, l> - H(s), and A(l) >= <r, l> + H(r) for each distribution r (Gibbs). Put r = s_x + a_x n. This gives KL >= H(r) - H(s_x) + a_x tau. The weighted sum of a_x tau is 0. Equality: s_x > 0 makes the fixed-n problem coercive in tau and l_x, since a large |tau| forces some q_x[i] to 0. So a minimiser exists. Its stationarity in l_x gives s_x - q_x parallel to n, so q_x = s_x + a_x n. Its stationarity in tau gives sum p_x a_x = 0. Also KL(s_x || q_x) = H(q_x) - H(s_x) + a_x <n, l_x>. The weighted sum of the last term is 0. QED.

statements.statement: Proposition A2 (the sharing term, any J, any family size f). Label the C = J f classes by a grid (b, j): b the family, j the position. Let s_x(b), s_x(j) be the row's marginals, and I_x = KL(s_x || s_x(b) s_x(j)), the mutual information of family and position in row x. Let A be the span of functions alpha(b) + gamma(j). Its dimension modulo 1 is J + f - 2. Then: (1) L_free(J + f - 2) <= sum p_x I_x. (2) If sum p_x (s_x - q_x) = 0, with q_x = s_x(b) s_x(j), then the least at the fixed span A is exactly sum p_x I_x. (3) For any row and any family b0: I_x = sum over b != b0 of s_x(b) KL(s_x(.|b) || s_x(.|b0)) - KL(s_x(.) || s_x(.|b0)). So I_x <= the cross-family mass times the KL of the cross-family contrast against the row's own contrast. (4) Reuse: the span A saves (J - 1)(f - 1) units against J + f - 2 + (J - 1)(f - 1) = C - 1. Its price is sum p_x I_x. The price is 0 exactly when every row is a product of family and position.
statements.proof: (1) log q_x is additive, so it lies in the span of 1 and A. Take t = 0. The loss is sum p_x KL(s_x || q_x). (2) s_x - q_x is orthogonal to A, since marginals agree. With r_x = q_x in the Gibbs step of A1, any logits in t + A satisfy D >= sum p_x [H(q_x) - H(s_x)] + sum p_x <q_x - s_x, t>. The last term is 0 by the premise. Also KL(s_x || q_x) = H(q_x) - H(s_x) because s_x - q_x is orthogonal to log q_x. (3) I_x = sum_b s_x(b) KL(s_x(.|b) || s_x(.)). The compensation identity: sum_b w_b KL(P_b || R) = sum_b w_b KL(P_b || Pbar) + KL(Pbar || R). Put R = s_x(.|b0). (4) KL = 0 exactly when s_x equals the product. QED.

statements.statement: Proposition A3 (a bound that charges for sharing). Let H_1, ..., H_J partition the classes. Let SHARE(w) = inf over t, V (C x w), c of sum_b sum_x p_x s_x(H_b) KL(s_x | H_b || softmax((t + V c_x) | H_b)). So all families use one code c_x. Then: (1) sum_b L^(b)(w) <= SHARE(w) <= L_Z(w) for any Z when SHARE uses codes in Z. (2) L_free(w + J - 1) <= SHARE(w) at free codes. (3) SHARE(w) = 0 exactly when w >= the affine rank of the rows of the matrix Lambda with entries log s_x(i) minus the mean of log s_x over the family of i. So the units reuse saves are sum_b (|H_b| - 1) minus that rank. SHARE is a bound device, not a new objective.
statements.proof: (1) Chain rule over classes (as in TQ22): KL(s_x || softmax(l_x)) = KL of family masses + sum_b s_x(H_b) KL(conditional || conditional). The first term is >= 0. Keep the competitor common, which gives the right side. Separating the codes gives the left side. (2) For a given (t, V, c), add one column per family except one, with free per-row codes. Choose them so that the family masses of softmax equal s_x(H_b). Conditionals do not change. The between-family KL is 0, and the rank rises by J - 1. (3) All weights are positive, since s_x > 0. So a zero needs softmax on H_b equal to s_x | H_b for all x and b. That says each row of Lambda lies in an affine space of dimension w, in the family-centred coordinates. Conversely, a rank-w factorisation of Lambda gives V, c, t. QED.
