statements.statement: Theorem A (four classes, two units, rows need not be symmetric). Label classes and rows by Z2^2 with xor. Let utilde = (1,1,-1,-1), vtilde = (1,-1,1,-1), wtilde = (1,-1,-1,1), and u, v, w these over 2. For any distribution r on 4 classes, r minus the product of its bit marginals equals Det(r) wtilde, with Det(r) = r_0 r_3 - r_1 r_2. So a table and a labelling fix q_x = the product of marginals of s_x, and bit logits with q_x = softmax(a_x utilde + b_x vtilde). Premises: (T1) 4 p_x Det(s_x) = nu wtilde_x for all x, with one nu > 0. (T2) <a, wtilde> = <b, wtilde> = 0. Let rho_j = min over x of p_x q_x(x xor j). (T3) nu / 2 <= rho_j for j = 0, 1, 2. Let phi(y) = (1 + y) log(1 + y) - y, gamma_j = 4 rho_j phi(-nu / (2 rho_j)), h = |<a, v> + <b, u>| / 2, K_T = gamma_0 + gamma_1 + gamma_2 + (8/3) rho_3 phi(3 nu / (4 rho_3)). (T4) 2 nu (<a, u> - h) >= K_T and 2 nu (<b, v> - h) >= K_T. Conclusion: L_free(2) = sum p_x [H(q_x) - H(s_x)] = sum p_x I_x > 0, attained by the span (u, v) with codes (2a, 2b). With strict T4, the span of (1, u, v) is the only such span of a minimiser. T1 to T4 are sufficient, not necessary.
statements.proof: Upper side: s_x - q_x = (nu / p_x) w_x w is orthogonal to log q_x, which lies in the span of 1, u, v. So KL(s_x || q_x) = H(q_x) - H(s_x), and this equals I_x. It is above 0 since nu > 0. Lower side: take any competitor. By A1 it has a unit normal n, with coordinates n_u, n_v, n_w, and class entries m. Let X_u = n_u^2, X_v = n_v^2, X_w = n_w^2, t = X_u + X_v. Dual point: r_x = s_x - (nu / p_x) m_x n. It has sum p_x (r_x - s_x) = -nu (sum m_x) n = 0, so the Gibbs step gives D >= sum p_x [H(r_x) - H(s_x)]. Also r_x = q_x - (nu / p_x) E_x, with E_xi = m_x m_i - w_x w_i. Entry facts, from sum m = 0 and |m| = 1: m_x^2 <= 3/4. For x != i, (m_x + m_i)^2 = (m_k + m_l)^2 <= 2 (1 - m_x^2 - m_i^2) <= 2 - (m_x + m_i)^2, so m_x m_i <= 1/4. And m_x m_i >= -1/2. Row formulas (sympy exact), with e_u = n_v n_w, e_v = n_u n_w, e_w = n_u n_v: E_(x,x) = (utilde_x e_u + vtilde_x e_v + wtilde_x e_w) / 2, E_(x,x+1) = (X_u - utilde_x e_u) / 2, E_(x,x+2) = (X_v - vtilde_x e_v) / 2, E_(x,x+3) = -T_x, with T_x = (t + wtilde_x e_w) / 2. So the first three kinds are <= 1/2, and 0 <= T_x <= 3/4. Positivity: T3 and these bounds give r_x >= 0. Expansion: eta(q + d) = eta(q) - (log q + 1) d - q phi(d / q), and rows of E sum to 0. So sum p_x [H(r_x) - H(q_x)] = Lin - Pen. Lin = nu sum_x m_x <log q_x, n> = 2 nu [<a,u> X_u + (<a,v> + <b,u>) n_u n_v + <b,v> X_v], using T2. With |n_u n_v| <= t / 2: Lin >= 2 nu [(<a,u> - h) X_u + (<b,v> - h) X_v]. Pen is the sum over x, i of p q phi(-nu E / (p q)). For E <= 1/2: phi(y) / y^2 is decreasing and rho phi(-z / rho) is decreasing in rho, so each term is at most gamma_j E^2. Sums over x: of E_(x,x)^2 is X_w t + X_u X_v <= t, of E_(x,x+1)^2 is X_u^2 + X_v X_w <= t, of E_(x,x+2)^2 is X_v^2 + X_u X_w <= t. At the partner: rho phi(z / rho) is decreasing in rho, and phi is convex with phi(0) = 0, so the term is at most (4 T_x / 3) rho_3 phi(3 nu / (4 rho_3)). And sum T_x = 2 t. So Pen <= K_T t. Then Lin - Pen >= X_u (2 nu (<a,u> - h) - K_T) + X_v (2 nu (<b,v> - h) - K_T) >= 0. Uniqueness: strict T4 makes this positive unless t = 0, that is n = w or -w. Rank-deficient competitors would need all extensions to have normal w, which is impossible. QED.

Let x = f_0 f_3 - f_1 f_2 = e (1-e)(y - z) > 0 and q = f + x(-1,1,1,-1). Test T: 2x <= q_0, q_1, q_2, and 2x log(q_j / q_3) >= q_0 phi(-2x/q_0) + q_1 phi(-2x/q_1) + q_2 phi(-2x/q_2) + (2/3) q_3 phi(3x/q_3) for j = 1, 2. Under T: L_free(2) = h(f_0 + f_1) + h(f_0 + f_2) - H(f) = (1-e) kl(y || m) + e kl(z || m) = e kl(z || y) - kl(m || y), with h the binary entropy. The least holds one family unit u and one shared unit v that writes +1 on a1, b1 and -1 on a2, b2. T holds whenever f_0 >= 11 f_3, f_1 >= 3 f_3, f_2 >= 3 f_3, and eta = (1 - f_0) + f_1 f_2 / f_3 <= 3/5. Sharing is free (loss 0 at k = 2 < 3 = C - 1) exactly when y = z. The benefit against the build with one own unit per family and no family unit is, in nats: h(lambda_w) - h(lambda_u), with lambda_u = f_0 + f_1 - f_2 - f_3, lambda_w = f_0 - f_1 - f_2 + f_3, h(lambda) = binary entropy of (1 + lambda)/2. Also 4x = lambda_w - lambda_u lambda_v.

The closed forms: q is the product of bit marginals, and the last form is Proposition A2 part 3. Explicit conditions: x = f_3 (1 - eta) <= f_3. Put q_3 = eta f_3, q_3 + 3x = (3 - 2 eta) f_3, q_j >= (4 - eta) f_3 for j = 1, 2, and q_0 >= 10 x. Direct algebra: 2x log(q_j/q_3) - (2/3) q_3 phi(3x/q_3) = 2x [log(q_j / (q_3 + 3x)) + 1] - x Omega(eta), with Omega = (2/3)(eta/(1-eta)) log((3 - 2 eta)/eta). q_j / (q_3 + 3x) >= (4 - eta)/(3 - 2 eta) >= 4/3. Omega has positive derivative on (0, 3/5], because its sign is that of log((3-2 eta)/eta) - 3(1-eta)/(3-2 eta), and the log is at least log 3 > 1 >= the second term. So Omega <= log 3. q phi(-2x/q) = 2x phi(-xi)/xi with xi = 2x/q, and phi(-xi)/xi is increasing. For j = 1, 2: xi <= 1/2, so the term is at most 2x (1 - log 2). For j = 0: xi <= 1/5, so it is at most 2x (1 + 4 log .8). Total: left side >= x (2 + 2 log(4/3) - log 3) = 1.4768 x. Right side <= 1.4423 x. QED. Free case: x = 0 makes each row a product. statements.statement: Proposition A4 (flat sharing is not always the least). On the translation table, n = cos(theta) w + sin(theta) v normal, M = f_0 + f_1, y = f_0/M, z = f_2/(1-M), m = f_0 + f_2, vbar = m(1-m), delta = log(m/(1-m)). Then Phi(theta) = (R(rho) + R(-rho))/2, with rho = log((1 + tan theta)/(1 - tan theta)) and R(rho) = min over d of M kl(y || sigma(d)) + (1-M) kl(z || sigma(e^rho d)). Also Phi''(0) = 4 M (1-M) / vbar times (vbar delta + m - z)(vbar delta + m - y). So if this product is negative, the character w is not the least. Instance: f = (.6, .38, .018, .002), with x < 0. It has product -0.0201, and L_free(2) is strictly below all three character values. At x > 0 the condition reads x <= q_0 q_1 log(q_0/q_1) / (q_0 + q_1).
statements.proof: n = alpha (e_0 - e_1) + beta (e_2 - e_3), with the family direction u kept. So family masses are matched and the chain rule splits each row's KL into two blocks. tau = 0, since row pairs flip both contrasts and the problem is convex in tau. The constraint is d_B = r d_A with r = (1 + tan theta)/(1 - tan theta). Row 0 gives R(rho). Row 2 gives M kl(y || sigma(r d)) + (1-M) kl(z || sigma(d)), and d -> d / r shows this is R(-rho). Envelope formula, with F the inner function and g_z(d) = kl(z || sigma(d)), g_z' = sigma - z, g_z'' = sigma(1-sigma): at rho = 0, sigma(d*) = m, F_dd = vbar, F_rho_rho = (1-M)(vbar delta^2 + (m-z) delta), F_d_rho = (1-M)(vbar delta + m - z). So R'' = F_rho_rho - F_d_rho^2 / F_dd = ((1-M)/vbar)(vbar delta + m - z)[M vbar delta - (1-M)(m-z)]. Since (1-M)(m-z) = M (y-m), R'' = (M(1-M)/vbar)(vbar delta + m - z)(vbar delta + m - y). rho = 2 theta + O(theta^3) gives Phi'' = 4 R''. For x > 0: y - m = x/M, and M vbar = q_0 q_1/(q_0 + q_1). Instance: the product is negative at w, and w has the least character value, so moving theta lowers the loss. QED.

statements.statement: Proposition A5 (a barrier for every dual point with fixed rows, free codes). Let (t, V, c) be a build with row errors G_x = p_x (s_x - q_x), and complement projector Pi_0 of rank m, 1 <= m <= C - 2. Take any matrix R, not depending on the competitor, with R Pi_0 = G, and the dual r_x = s_x - (R Pi)_x / p_x, as in TQ17, TQ18 and Theorem A. If r_x >= 0 at every projector Pi of rank m with Pi 1 = 0, then for each row and any two classes i != j: |s_x - q_x|_2 <= (s_x(i) + s_x(j)) / c_C, with c_C = sqrt(1 - 1/C) - sqrt(1/2 - 1/C), c_4 = .366, c_C -> .293. So the row's fit error is at most about 3.4 times the sum of its two smallest probabilities.
statements.proof: Let r' be row x of R and e' be e_i, both projected off 1. If r' = 0 then G_x = 0 and the claim holds. Let b be the unit bisector of r' and e' (if they are opposite, the next quantity is 0 and the bound is trivial). Let Pi = b b^T plus m - 1 unit directions orthogonal to 1, r', e', which exist since m <= C - 2. Then (R Pi)_(x,i) = <r', b><b, e'> = (|r'||e'| + <r', e'>)/2. r_x(i) >= 0 gives this <= p_x s_x(i). Add the same for j: |r'||e'| + <r', e'_i + e'_j>/2 <= p_x (s_x(i) + s_x(j)). Use <r', e'_i + e'_j> >= -|r'| sqrt(2 - 4/C), with |e'|^2 = 1 - 1/C. This gives |r'| c_C <= p_x (s_x(i) + s_x(j)). Finally |G_x| = |Pi_0 r'| <= |r'|. QED. It is a statement about this form of proof, not about the least.

result.track: C: tail order and sign rank
result.summary: I have two lower bounds on the least loss that hold for every competitor span and name no build: a cut bound from Forster's theorem that pays in the mass of misordered sibling pairs, and a packing dual from weighted (Lewis) positions that pays when a table lifts a class in its own row against k units. On a confident table with a level tail the packing dual holds about 30% of a fit at k = 14, K = 64, at every confidence I tried from e = 0.3 to 0.001, and on family-tree tails it holds 1% to 16% where the sibling minors of TQ22 give 0 (and 0 in 2 of the 6 tables at k = 14). No slot is filled: nothing here is exact, the bound is not first-order tight, it gives each block all k units, order data alone cannot see the rank of a family tree at k >= 2 (proved), and nothing was measured on a real network.

statements.statement: Lemma C1 (pairs, fractional). Let y_p >= 0 on pairs of classes with the sum over pairs holding class i at most 1, for each i. For positive distributions s, q: KL(s||q) >= sum over p of y_p (s_i + s_j) kl(alpha_p || beta_p), with alpha_p = s_i/(s_i+s_j), beta_p = q_i/(q_i+q_j).
statements.proof: Add singleton blocks with weight 1 minus the pair sum at each class. The blocks B then cover each class with total weight 1. So KL = sum y_B s(B) log(s(B)/q(B)) + sum y_B s(B) KL(s|B || q|B). The weights y_B s(B) and y_B q(B) each sum to 1, so the first sum is >= 0 by Gibbs. Singletons add 0 to the second sum. QED. A fractional matching need not be a mixture of matchings, because of odd cycles. This proof does not use that step.

statements.statement: Lemma C3 (Forster, error form, weighted). Let M be n x m with entries +-1, x and w distributions on rows and columns, w_p <= 1/r, nu = |D_x^(1/2) M D_w^(1/2)|_op. For every real Z of rank at most r, the mass under x tensor w of the entries with M Z <= 0 is at least (1/r - nu)/2.
statements.proof: First let w_p = n_p/N be rational. Then n_p <= N/r. Write Z = U V^T in R^r. Let E be the set with M Z <= 0. Replace column p by n_p copies. Perturb all copies into general position, keep the strict signs off E, and keep rows nonzero. By Forster 2002 (recalled, not re-checked) an invertible A exists with the sum over the N copies of (Av)(Av)^T/|Av|^2 equal to (N/r) I. Let v' = Av/|Av| and u' = A^-T u/|A^-T u|. Signs do not change. For each row, (1/N) sum |<u',v'>| >= (1/N) sum <u',v'>^2 = 1/r, since |<u',v'>| <= 1. Off E, M<u',v'> = |<u',v'>|. On E, M<u',v'> >= |<u',v'>| - 2. So sum x (1/N) M <u',v'> >= 1/r - 2 mass(E). The left side is a sum over coordinates of alpha^T B beta, with |B|_op = nu, sum |alpha|^2 = 1, sum |beta|^2 = 1, so it is at most nu. For real w: rational points are dense in the polytope {0 <= w <= 1/r, sum = 1}, and both sides are continuous. QED. The premise w <= 1/r is enough because the perturbation gives general position.

statements.statement: Theorem C4 (cut bound). Let R be rows and Q pairs (i_p, j_p), y_c(p) a fractional matching in each row, D_cp = log(s_c[i_p]/s_c[j_p]), alpha_cp = sigma(D_cp), a_cp = s_c[i_p] + s_c[j_p]. Let I_p = [th-_p, th+_p] be intervals and M_cp signs with M = +1 implying D_cp >= th+_p and M = -1 implying D_cp <= th-_p. Let th_p(s) = th-_p + s|I_p|. Let x, w be distributions with w_p <= 1/(k+1), and nu as in C3. Let g_cp(s) = p_c y_c(p) a_cp |I_p| |sigma(th_p(s)) - alpha_cp|, and lambda(s) the least over x_c w_p > 0 of g_cp(s)/(x_c w_p). Then L_free(k) >= (1/2)(1/(k+1) - nu)_+ times the integral over s in [0,1] of lambda(s). No competitor is fixed. Parts: disjoint rectangles add.
statements.proof: Write d_cp = l_c[i] - l_c[j] = (t_i - t_j) + (V_i - V_j).c_c. C1 bounds the row's KL by the sum of y a kl(alpha||sigma(d)). C2 gives, for M = +1, kl >= |I_p| times the integral of (alpha - sigma(th_p(s))) 1[d <= th_p(s)] ds, because th+_p <= D and the integrand is >= 0 below D. M = -1 is the mirror case. Z(s) = d - th_p(s) has rank at most k+1, because a column shift enters the offset t. Apply C3 at each s, with g >= lambda x w. Integrate. QED.

statements.statement: Corollary C4.1 (tilted family table). Let H be N x N with H H^T = N I. C = K = 2N. Families b hold two siblings i_(b,+), i_(b,-). Row (b,sig) has p = 1/(2N), s[i_(b,sig)] = 1 - eps, s[i_(b,-sig)] = eps0, log((1-eps)/eps0) >= 2 eta, and for b' != b, s[i_(b',tau)] = a_bb' exp(tau eta H_bb')/(2 cosh eta), with a_bb' >= a. a_bb' may grow with relatedness. Then L_free(k) >= N a kl(sigma(2 eta) || 1/2) (1/(k+1) - 1/sqrt N - sqrt 2/N)_+.

statements.statement: Lemma C8 (floored Lewis weights). Let U be n x r of full column rank with rows u_j, and x0 > 0. Then x_j >= x0 exist with M = sum u_j u_j^T/x_j and x_j^2 = u_j^T M^-1 u_j + x0^2. Let T_jl = u_j^T M^-1 u_l/(x_j x_l) and R = xi(D_x^-1 - T). Then: (a) sum x_j <= r + n x0. (b) T is psd of rank <= r, T_jj = 1 - x0^2/x_j^2, |T_jl| <= 1. (c) x_l T_ll <= 1, so 0 <= R_ll <= xi/x0. (d) R is symmetric, R U = 0, and R 1 = 0 if 1 lies in the range of U. (e) sum over j of x_j T_jl^2 = T_ll. (f) sum over j != l of T_jl^2 <= sum over l of (1/x_l - T_ll) = tr R/xi.
statements.proof: Let Phi(A) = 2 sum sqrt(u_j^T A u_j + x0^2) - log det A on A > 0. Rows span, so c = the least over unit e of max_j |<u_j,e>| is above 0, and Phi >= 2c sqrt(lambda_max) - r log lambda_max. Also -log det A tends to +inf as lambda_min tends to 0 at bounded lambda_max. So a minimiser exists. Stationarity gives sum u_j u_j^T/x_j = A^-1 with x_j = sqrt(u_j^T A u_j + x0^2), so M = A^-1. (a) r = tr(M^-1 M) = sum (x_j^2 - x0^2)/x_j, so sum x_j = r + x0^2 sum 1/x_j <= r + n x0. (b) T = D^-1 U M^-1 U^T D^-1 is psd, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives |T_jl| <= sqrt(T_jj T_ll). (c) D^(1/2) T D^(1/2) is an orthogonal projector, because M = U^T D^-1 U. Its diagonal is x_l T_ll. (d) R U = xi(D^-1 U - D^-1 U M^-1 M) = 0. (e) Direct, from the definition of M. (f) 1 <= (x_j/x_l + x_l/x_j)/2, and T is symmetric, so the sum of T_jl^2 is at most the sum of T_jl^2 x_j/x_l, which is sum_l T_ll/x_l by (e). Subtract the diagonal: T_ll(1/x_l - T_ll) <= 1/x_l - T_ll by (b), (c). QED. At x0 = 0 these are Lewis's weights (Lewis 1978, recalled, not re-checked), and the rows are in Forster's radial isotropic position with weights x.

statements.statement: Theorem C9 (peak bound in L1). Let W be a subspace of R^n of dimension r, and f_i in W with f_i(i) = m_i > 0, for i = 1..n. Then the sum over i of |f_i|_1 is at least (sum over i of sqrt m_i)^2 / r. Equality holds at n = r g, W = functions constant on r groups of size g, f_i = m times the indicator of i's group.
statements.proof: Let U be a basis of W, f = U e. Let a_c = u_i^T M^-1 u_c/x_c. Then sum over c of a_c f(c) = u_i^T M^-1 M e = f(i), and |a_c| <= x_i by (b). So m_i <= x_i |f_i|_1. Cauchy-Schwarz gives sum m_i/x_i >= (sum sqrt m_i)^2/sum x_i, and sum x_i <= r + n x0 by (a). Let x0 tend to 0. Equality: direct. QED. Read as a network: for any k units, lifting each class by m in its own row moves that class's column by a mean of at least m/(k + 1) per row, in total over the two signs. The extremal span is coarse equal groups. An absorber row cannot make this cheap for all classes at once.

statements.statement: Theorem C10 (packing dual). Rows x, weights p_x, s_x > 0 on C classes; kept part of dimension y (y = 1 if none); r = y + k. A block S is a list of n pairs (x_j, i_j), rows distinct, classes distinct. Premise: no pair (x, i) is a diagonal pair of one block and an off-diagonal pair of another. Block numbers: Y_jl = log s_(x_j)[i_l]; for any vectors a, g, Ybar = Y - a 1^T - 1 g^T; m_S = min_j Ybar_jj; A_S = the off-diagonal part of Ybar, symmetrised; |A|_(r) = (sum over j <= r of sigma_j(A)^2)^(1/2). Parameters b in (0,1], x0 > 0, kappa_b = phi(-b)/b^2, k'' = r + n x0, m' = m_S - 1 - kappa_b b. G_S(k) = m'(n^2/k'' - n) - (n/sqrt k'')|A_S|_(r). Let xi_S >= 0, with xi_S = 0 where G_S <= 0 or n <= k'', such that for each off-diagonal pair (x,i) the sum of xi_S over blocks holding it is at most b p_x s_x[i], and for each diagonal pair at most x0 p_x s_x[i]. Then L_Z(k) >= L_free(k) >= the sum over S of xi_S G_S(k).
statements.proof: Fix a competitor. Let U_S be a basis of the span of Y and the codes restricted to the rows of S. 1 is in its range, and its rank is at most r. C8 gives x, T, R^S with xi = xi_S. Let R be the sum of the R^S on (row, class) pairs. Domain: off-diagonal |R| <= sum xi_S <= b p s, and on the diagonal 0 <= R <= sum xi_S/x0 <= p s. Row sums of R are 0 by (d). So q°_x = s_x - R_x/p_x is a distribution. Each column of R^S is orthogonal to the restricted logit column of its class by (d), so sum over x of <R_x, l_x> = 0. TQ13 part 1 gives D >= sum p_x (H(q°_x) - H(s_x)), and (E) of TQ17 makes this <log s, R> - sum p s phi(-R/(p s)). Diagonal cost: with y = R/(ps) in [0,1], ps phi(-y) <= ps y^2 <= R. Off-diagonal cost: ps phi(-R/ps) <= kappa_b R^2/(ps), since phi(y)/y^2 is decreasing and y >= -b. R^2 <= (sum xi_S)(sum xi_S (T^S)^2), and sum xi_S <= b ps. So the cost is at most kappa_b b sum xi_S (T^S_jl)^2, and by (f) its block total is at most kappa_b b tr R^S. Gain: R^S has zero row and column sums, so <log s, R^S> = <Ybar, R^S> >= m_S tr R^S - xi_S <A_S, T>, since the diagonal of R^S is >= 0 and off it R^S = -xi_S T. T has rank <= r, so <A_S,T> <= |A_S|_(r)|T|_F <= |A_S|_(r) sqrt(Sigma), Sigma = sum 1/x_l, by von Neumann and (f). Net of a block: xi_S[m'(Sigma - sum T_ll) - sqrt(Sigma)|A_S|_(r)] >= xi_S h(Sigma), with h(Sigma) = m'(Sigma - n) - sqrt(Sigma)|A_S|_(r). By Cauchy-Schwarz and (a), Sigma >= n^2/k''. h is quadratic in sqrt Sigma with vertex |A|/(2m'). G_S > 0 forces m' > 0 and n/sqrt k'' > |A|/m'. So h is increasing past n^2/k'', and h >= G_S there. If the span has lower rank, each term only improves. QED. It uses no stationary triple, no pinned span, no test such as g <= rho, and no projector fixed in advance: the dual point changes with the competitor and stays a distribution by the two entry limits. A tiny entry excludes only the blocks that hold it.

statements.statement: Proposition C6 (order alone cannot see the rank of a family tree). Let K = C = 2^d and s_c[i] = g(lev(c,i)), with g strictly decreasing in the level of the lowest common ancestor (top class at level 0). (1) At k = 1 a logit table orders every strict pair of every row correctly: x_i = sum over j of bit_j(i) 2 3^-j, c_c = x_c, V_i = 2 x_i, t_i = -x_i^2. (2) Every value of Theorem C4 is 0 at k >= 2, for all pairs, intervals, weights and blocks. Premises: exactly those. It holds on clean tables with relatives likelier than strangers, and with any confidence in the top class.
statements.proof: (1) l_c[i] - l_c[j] = (x_c - x_j)^2 - (x_c - x_i)^2. If lev(c,i) < lev(c,j), let p be the first bit where c and j differ. Then |x_c - x_j| >= 3^-p and |x_c - x_i| < 3^-p. (2) Let w = LCA(i,j). Outside w's subtree, D = 0. In i's child, D > 0, and it depends only on lev(c,i), falling as lev(c,i) grows. In j's child the mirror holds. So {D > th} is a subtree for th >= 0 and the complement of a subtree for th < 0. Each is an interval or co-interval of the x order, so a quadratic in x_c has that sign on the support: rank 3. C3 with no errors gives nu >= 1/3. So 1/(k+1) - nu <= 0 at k >= 2. QED. This does not say a slot is unfillable. It says a bound that reads only order and thresholds cannot fill Slot 3 on tree tables, so Radon, sign rank, margin on order data, and sign-pattern counting need magnitudes there.

statements.statement: Proposition C5 (counting, random tilt). Let M be uniform +-1, n x m, V = r(n+m), 2nm >= V. If h <= 1/2 and (16 e n m/V)^V 2^(-nm(1 - H2(h))) <= delta, then with probability at least 1 - delta every Z of rank <= r has M Z <= 0 on at least h n m entries. Used in Theorem C4 with x, w uniform, the factor (1/r - nu)/2 becomes h.
statements.proof: Alon 1995 (recalled, not re-checked): nm degree-2 polynomials in V variables have at most (16 e n m/V)^V sign patterns in {-,0,+}. Fix a pattern. Fill zeros with any sign. The event that the error count with ties is at most h n m lies in the event that M is within Hamming distance h n m of the filled pattern, of probability at most 2^(-nm(1 - H2(h))). Union bound. QED.

statements.statement: Proposition C7 (Radon form). If k + 2 rows are shattered by (pair, threshold) columns, every competitor of rank k misorders an entry on those rows. The pay d_cp - th_p is affine in the code, so it cannot be > 0 on all of A and <= 0 on all of B. Pay the wrong entry by C1 and C2. The minimum over bipartitions removes the dependence on the competitor. QED.

verdicts.statement: E1 (T = sum p r (J log s)^T = lambda W W^T, the trace identity, sign bounds, rank T = affine rank of the logits, the triple identities, the form with decay on b).
verdicts.gaps: I checked every part by hand, parts (1) to (8). There is one loose step in (7). T = sum p r (J l - J b)^T gives rank T <= dim span{W h_x}, not rank T <= affine rank. Use a centre c in the affine hull of the J l_x: by (1), T = sum p r (J l - c)^T. Then the chain closes. Part (4) also holds for soft labels. Part (7) is false with decay on b: T = lambda (W W^T + b b^T), and rank T can be rank W + 1 when b is not in range W. Part (7) is stated only without decay, but torchvision-style training usually decays b, so eps_T must use the decay form on such a net. The remark 'no exact rational solution exists' has no proof. The word 'new' rests on a grep only; my grep also found no earlier form.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, with the centre c in the proof of (7), and (7) only with no decay on b.

verdicts.statement: E2 (a positive table with balance, T symmetric positive semidefinite, and the range condition is the output of an exactly stationary all-on ReLU net at every lambda and depth; at m = 1 a local minimum and the global least among all-on nets; the soft-label corollary).
verdicts.gaps: I checked the gradient exponents, the zero moments on the hard-label coordinates, the nuclear-norm subgradient lambda Q, and the corollary. My own net at tree levels [20,0,3,0], one label per row: gradient 3.5e-14, table error 3e-22. Limits to say plainly: every unit is on at every row, so the net is linear on P. So 'nothing more is forced' is a statement about a net with free inputs and no gates. The count C(C-1)/2 is right only if it includes balance: symmetry alone gives (C-1)(C-2)/2 equations, and balance gives C-1. T = 0 needs W = 0 as a separate trivial case.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, with 'forced' read as 'forced at the table on nets with free inputs'.

verdicts.statement: E3 (two exactly stationary nets share lambda, W W^T, p, label share, Hbar and CE, with L_free(1) <= eps^2/4 on one and >= c_0 on the other).
verdicts.false_step: The proof says Hbar(B_m) goes to 0 as m goes to infinity. This is false, because b keeps the mean of s uniform. Four rows cannot all be one-hot with mean (1/3, 1/3, 1/3) on 3 classes.
verdicts.counterexample: Over 13 basis angles, the least of Hbar(B_m) is 0.31826 at most angles and 0.39857 at the angle where the classes tie. That least is the limit at large m. At large m the rows are near e1, e2, (1/3, 0, 2/3), (0, 1/3, 2/3), and the mean entropy is 0.318, not 0. The root still exists: Hbar(A_eps) is in [0.555, 0.786] on the same grid (eps = 0.001, 0.4, 1).
verdicts.gaps: (1) The repair uses computed numbers, not a hand bound. (2) Per-row label shares differ between the two tables. In A_eps, r_x = lambda A (+-1/3, +-1/eps); in B, r_x differs. Only the p-mean label share is shared. So the theorem does not cover a function that reads per-row labels. (3) lambda_eps is O(eps). (4) The nets are all-on and the labels are tuned to the table, so this is not the clean, trained-like instance that the OR clause of the brief asks for. The author does not claim that clause. (5) The check says 'm = 3'. That is the first coordinate of xi. The root on the author's table is m = 1.4484. The other numbers reproduce: Hbar 0.660469, L_free(1) 0.003795 and 0.147499 by multistart.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Fix a basis A at which Hbar(A_0) exceeds L_inf(A), the limit of Hbar(B_m). At basis angle 0 these are 0.686 and 0.318. For all small enough eps, continuity gives Hbar(A_eps) in (L_inf(A), log 3), the intermediate value theorem gives m in a compact interval, and the rest of the proof holds. Then no function of (lambda, W W^T, p, p-mean label share, Hbar, CE) is within a bounded ratio of L_free(1). The conclusion for all eps in (0, 1] and all bases is computed on a grid only.

verdicts.statement: E4 (V_b(k) >= L_Z(k) >= L_free(k) >= min{(lambda E_k)^2 / (4 kappa), tau_0 lambda E_k / 2}, and the minor form).
verdicts.false_step: The first link of the written chain, V_b(k) >= L_Z(k), is false for Z = always-on read. TQ11 part 1 gives L_free <= V_b <= L_on, and E6 of the same report says V_b <= L_on.
verdicts.counterexample: z = -1, 0, 1, p = 1/3, C = 3, k = 1, s_x = softmax(relu(z) v), v = (1, -1, 0). One unit relu(z) fits exactly, so V_b(1) = 0. The problem for L_on(1) is convex, and its least is 0.016470 (0.069367 with scale 3 on the logit).
verdicts.gaps: The rest of the proof holds by hand: the dual point, Ky Fan with W^T 1 = 0, the chi-square bound and the choice of tau. The minor form also holds; the leak term is absent, as claimed. It needs k <= |H| - 2 to say anything. The bound is not tight, as the author says.
verdicts.corrected_statement: min{(lambda E_k)^2 / (4 kappa), tau_0 lambda E_k / 2} <= L_free(k) <= min(V_b(k), L_on(k)).

verdicts.statement: E5 (if s - Pi u is a distribution for every rank-m projector, then |u|_2 <= 2 s_(2) / ((1 - 1/sqrt 2)(1 - 1/C)^(1/2)) <= 8.4 s_(2)).
verdicts.gaps: I checked the bisector step and the two-class step by hand. TQ17 fits, since q° = s_c - mu_c Pi e_c. TQ18 at Z = R^n fits, since G° = R Pi. The premise is narrower than it needs to be. Random projectors agree with the formula at C = 3, m = 1 (0.5407 vs 0.5407) and C = 4, m = 2 (0.3176 vs 0.3177). u must be fixed for all Pi; see the next entry.
verdicts.corrected_statement: The same bound holds for C >= 3 and 1 <= m <= C - 2, so it also covers k = 1.

verdicts.statement: E5's glosses and the blocked_by text: 'the limit of any dual point linear in one projector', 'all duals linear in one projector', 'level tails were the only family', and 'for free codes the moment dual and the row dual are the same, so the tiny number returns'.
verdicts.false_step: E5 proves a limit only for q(Pi) = s - Pi u with u fixed. A dual point can be affine in Pi and have another form. A competitor-dependent u(Pi) is also outside it.
verdicts.counterexample: E6's own dual q°_x = q_x - Cov(q_x) Psi^-1[(Pi - Pi_0) R] zeta_x is affine in Pi and is a distribution at every Pi. My table A has s min 1.4e-22 and loss 4.5e-8, so |s - q| is of order 1e-4 on average (Pinsker), far above tail-scale limits. TQ18 part 4 is an exact family with graded tails, so level tails are not the only family. At a fixed span, the best build's softmax is an exact dual point with no positivity cost, and its u depends on Pi.
verdicts.gaps: That the free-code wall is real is expected, not proved. No theorem here excludes a free-code dual that is nonlinear in Pi. The author's next step does name this open dual, which conflicts with 'the tiny number returns'.
verdicts.corrected_statement: A certificate that reaches real tables must not have the form s_x - Pi u_x with u_x fixed. Nothing is proved about other forms.

verdicts.statement: E6 (moment certificate: under g <= eta sigma / 2 and 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max <= eta the triple is the global least for L_Z(k); the graded part (2); part (3)).
verdicts.gaps: I checked steps (a) to (g) by hand, and they hold. My own tables, built by a separate script: C = 6, D = 6, k = 2, s min 1.4e-22 and 2.8e-49, top 0.83 and 0.92, TQ18 test off by 4.6e18 and 2.4e44. Best competitor minus D0 stayed above 0 (+4e-16 to +3e-15). Part (3) is not new: the Comment of TQ18 already says what the read cannot compute costs nothing. It is a certificate of L_on only, since V_b <= L_on. A triple names a build, so no slot 1. Losses at the test are about 1e-9 to 2e-7 unless an unread part is added.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, for L_on and region tables only, not free codes, not the gated box.

verdicts.statement: The summary's claim on E6: 'a certificate for the always-on read with no tiny probability in it'.
verdicts.false_step: eta carries tiny probabilities whenever one read direction can sit on rows where a class is tiny. This is a property of the read, not of the theorem.
verdicts.counterexample: D = 6, n = 600, C = 6, k = 2, top mean 0.917. One read coordinate lives only on 264 rows where class 1 is at most 8.9e-13. Then eta = 6.4e-14. The test caps g at or below that scale. With a cut at 1e-24, eta reaches the float floor of about 1e-17 to 1e-19, so that value is not resolved.
verdicts.gaps: How small eta is on a real read is not known. Within-class directions of z may reach small values. The lower bound eta >= least q also holds.
verdicts.corrected_statement: For every class i and unit w in R^D: eta <= (C/(C-1)) sum p_x q_x[i](1 - q_x[i])(w . zeta_x)^2 <= (C/(C-1)) max of q_x[i] over rows with w . zeta_x != 0. So rho is replaced by the least read-weighted mean of a class's probability. This helps only on a read that cannot steer onto rows where a class is tiny.

verdicts.statement: E6-reach (Delta_k <= r g^2 / eta under E6's test, the cap of 1.7e-5 nats on ResNet-18 at k = 14, and the miss by 4 orders or more).
verdicts.false_step: The bound is proved only for r <= 2 k*. The use on ResNet-18 has r about 499 and 2 k* = 28, outside that range. The author marks it 'expected'.
verdicts.counterexample: I found none. Delta_k / (r g^2 / eta) was 0.002 to 0.026, including r = 6 > 2 k* = 2.
verdicts.gaps: The arithmetic is right: 1.74e-5 at k = 14; 1.5e-6 at k = 128 with r about 384. Units differ from TQ18's '1e23 to 1e78', which is a ratio in g. Since the cap is quadratic in g, 4 orders in loss is about 2.4 orders in g. The cap also uses the best possible eta = 1/(C-1) and zeta_max = sqrt D, so the true miss may be far larger. 'Far better than TQ18' is not shown.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Proved: under the test with r <= 2 k*, L_Z(k) - L_Z(C-1) <= <Gamma, Psi^-1 Gamma> <= r g^2 / eta. Beyond that range it stays a conjecture.

verdicts.statement: E7 (stationarity gives no relation with the always-on read: the twin-row proposition; scale-invariant layers have theta = 0, so exact stationarity holds only at the head).
verdicts.gaps: The twin-row proposition holds by hand. It needs |rho| small enough to keep labels in the simplex and rho orthogonal to 1. 'Only at the head' is too strong. A layer whose scale is not removed downstream can stay nonzero, for example the gain of the last BatchNorm in a residual block, because its output is added to a shortcut. The invariance holds for train-mode batch statistics, while N's table uses eval mode. This does not make eps_T nonzero by itself: T uses only the head's equations.
verdicts.corrected_statement: Every weight layer whose scale is removed by a later normalisation has theta = 0 at exact stationarity with lambda > 0. So F8 cannot hold exactly on such layers. The head and non-invariant parameters are not excluded by this argument.

verdicts.statement: E8 (D(l') >= tau (CE_R(l') - CE_R(N)) - sum p psi*; L_Z(k) >= sup over tau of [tau (C_Z,R(k) - CE_R(N)) - sum p psi*]; C_free(k) = 0 for k >= 2).

verdicts.gaps: psi*, its second derivative and b* hold by hand. The vacuity result is stronger than stated.
verdicts.corrected_statement: L_Z(k) >= the sup over tau in [0, theta) of the same expression. For free codes with a free offset, C_free(k) = 0 already at k = 1: tangent lines t_i = -rho i^2 / 2, slopes rho i, codes c = i give CE = 2.5e-11 at rho = 50, C = 12. So the bound is at most 0 for all k >= 1.

verdicts.false_step: 'The own-family entries dominate this, since their mass and gap are larger.' The gap is larger. The mass 1 - eps + eps0 need not be at least a. The table's premises do not force it.
verdicts.counterexample: N = 4, eps = 0.9, eta = 1, eps0 = (1 - eps) e^-2. Then a = 0.2955 and own-family mass = 0.1135, with equal gap. So lambda is 0.38 of what the proof uses. This breaks the proof, not the inequality. The claimed bound 0.0567 stays below a fit 0.305. In 5 cases, including N = 16, eps = 0.99, no violation of the stated inequality was found. Second fault: the reported check numbers are not this corollary's. t5_struct.py uses nu = 1/sqrt(N) on H alone. At N = 256, k = 14 the corollary gives 1/15 - 1/16 - sqrt(2)/256 = -0.0014, so 0, and not the reported .0042. At N = 64 it gives .853, .353, .103 and not .875, .375, .125.
verdicts.gaps: The statement itself is neither proved as written nor refuted. The denominators in the check come from the H-only pair minor, not from this table. The whole-table fit is far above the bound (1.54 against 0.0116 at N = 16, eps = 0.3, k = 1). I re-derived the rest: |M| <= sqrt(2N) + 2, nu <= 1/sqrt(N) + sqrt(2)/N, and the integral 2 N a kl(sigma(2 eta)||1/2).
verdicts.corrected_statement: Let h = 1/(k+1) - 1/sqrt(N) - sqrt(2)/N, and own = the least of 1 - eps + eps0 over rows. Then L_free(k) >= N kl0 x max( min(a, own) h_+ , a (h - 2/N)_+ ), kl0 = kl(sigma(2 eta)||1/2). The second term holds because own-family entries carry mass 1/N in total. If own >= a (for example any table with eps - eps0 <= (N-1)/N), the stated form holds. Same scope fix: k + 1 becomes y + k.

verdicts.statement: Theorem C10 (packing dual)
verdicts.gaps: I checked each step: domain, row sums, orthogonality, the diagonal and off-diagonal costs, the Cauchy step over blocks, von Neumann, the vertex of h, and the lower-rank case. Independent test: 2367 tables with LP weights, photo rows, overlap, kept parts, b < 1, nonzero A; 0 cases of bound > fit and 0 chain failures. Eight early domain flags near -3e-7 were LP tolerance; with normalised constraints 0 of 1307 flagged. Notation fault: Y names both the kept part and the block's log table. The kept part must contain 1. The largest bound / fit in my random tables was 0.12. It gives no claim with an error, so it fills no slot. Each block's U_S is free, as the author says. It uses |T| <= 1 on both signs, which costs a constant.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, with the two Y renamed. Complement, proved by me, same premises and same block list. For n > r let G'_S = (n - r)(m_S - 3) - sqrt(r) |A_S|_(r). Let xi_S >= 0, with xi_S = 0 where G'_S <= 0, the sum of xi_S on each off-diagonal pair at most 2 p s, and on each diagonal pair at most p s. Then L_free(k) >= the sum of xi_S G'_S. Proof: R^S = xi_S Pi_S, Pi_S the projector onto the complement of a dimension-r subspace of R^n that holds 1 and the restricted logit span. Pi_jl <= 1/2 off the diagonal, 0 <= Pi_jj <= 1, phi(u) <= u^2 on u >= -1, the sum of Pi^2 is n - r, and <A, Pi> = -<A, P> since A has zero diagonal. Tested: 1255 tables, 0 chain failures. It beat C10 on 521 tables, mostly where r > n/2.

verdicts.statement: Corollary C11 (level tail, any k)
verdicts.gaps: The bound is correct. 'Free codes when eps_const = 0' is an unneeded condition on K rows, since C10 gives L_free directly. The summary's 'about 30% at every confidence' holds only for the tested range and for that k. Warm-started fits, K = 64, k = 14: ratio .305 at m = 6.34, .287 at 11.05, .245 at m = 100. k = 7: .196 to .156. K = 32, k = 3: .107 to .082. Fits are upper values. This is the toy's world, so it fills no slot.
verdicts.corrected_statement: With r = k + 1 <= K, K >= 3 and 2 beta (K-1)/(K-2) <= a, also: L_free(k) >= (2 beta (K - r)/(K - 2)) (m - 2K/(K - 2)). Proof: fix a competitor. Let Pi be the projector onto the complement of a dimension-r subspace holding 1 and V, and R = xi Pi, xi = 2 beta/(K-2). Then Pi_ci <= 1/2 - 1/K gives R_ci <= beta/K, the premise gives R_cc <= a/K, <log s, R> = xi (K-r) m, and phi(u) <= u^2 gives cost at most (K/beta) xi^2 (K-r). Use the larger of this and C11; this one wins when k + 1 > K/2 - 1. At K = 2k it matches TQ17 at first order in m: exact is beta m + O(beta) and the bound is beta (m - 2K/(K-2)). Ratios at K = 64: m = 11: .897, m = 100: .990. C11's own limit there is only (K-2)/(K+2). Tested against fits at K = 6 to 24, all k, m = 3, 5, 8: 0 violations. Fitted slope against this slope at K = 16: k = 8: 1.000, 1.000; k = 14: .143, .143; k = 10: .750, .714; k = 7: 2.625, 1.143. So tightness is expected only for k >= K/2, and not proved beyond K = 2k.

verdicts.statement: Proposition C6 (order cannot see the rank of a family tree)
verdicts.gaps: Proof is right. Part 1 is exact arithmetic on the Cantor coordinates. Part 2 is right: every admissible sign pattern separates a subtree or its complement by an interval of x, so rows (1, x, x^2) realise it with rank 3. Scope is narrow in two ways. (a) Premises are exact level-only tails, a symmetric table, allowed only as a clean check. Noise on D outside the LCA subtree breaks the zero. (b) 'Order data alone' in the summary means one threshold per column at a time. C3 is applied at each s apart, and Z(s) shares one d. The statement is about bounds of C3's kind, not about all use of signs at several thresholds. Random check at d = 5: least nu found 0.60, above 1/3.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, on exact level-tail binary trees, for every value of C4 and any bound that applies C3 at one threshold per column. It says nothing about a noisy tree.

verdicts.statement: Proposition C5 (counting, random tilt)
verdicts.gaps: Holds given Alon 1995. Its source is recalled, by the author and by me, in the same form (8 e d m / l)^l for 2m >= l. The arithmetic checks: h about .186 at n = m = 1024, r = 15. Nothing at N = 256. No certificate, so it fails Slot 1, as the author says.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated, conditional on Alon's count.

verdicts.statement: Proposition C7 (Radon form)
verdicts.gaps: 'Pay' is not defined in the statement. It must be p_c y a kl(sigma(D) || sigma(th)), with th the column's threshold. It is above 0 only when D is off th, so a column needs a margin on both sides. With kept units k + 2 becomes y + k + 1. On level trees it is empty at k >= 2, since intervals and co-intervals shatter at most 3 rows.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated with pay defined as above and k + 2 replaced by y + k + 1.

verdicts.statement: Conjecture C12 (m^2 / (k+1) on the level tail)
verdicts.false_step: The rough check read fit/e growing faster than m as a power law. The growth is affine in m with a negative intercept. Example K = 64, k = 7: fit/e is about 0.72 m - 2.3. Local slope stays .68 to .73 from m = 8 to m = 100.
verdicts.counterexample: K = 64, k = 6, so also k = 7. Competitor l_ci = -m Ham(c,i). Then q_c is a product of 6 Bernoullis and KL has a closed form: L/e <= m (192/63 - 1) + 6/(a 63). Against RHS/e = c m^2 (3/4)/8, the allowed c is at most 1.07 at m = 20, .217 at m = 100, .036 at m = 600. The top class is kept at each m. So no absolute c > 0 exists. In general for any K and any k >= 1: x_i = i/(K-1), tau = m (K-1)^2, l_ci = -tau (x_c - x_i)^2 has rank 1 plus offset and margins at least m, so L/e <= m (mean over c != i of (c-i)^2 - 1) + O(1).
verdicts.gaps: The route 'lift the cap to reach m^2' in the author's next step (2) is closed. Using the sign of T buys a constant and not a power of m.
verdicts.corrected_statement: For fixed K and k >= 1: c1 e (m - O(1)) <= L_free(k) <= c2(K,k) e (m + O(1)), with c1 = (K-k-1)/((K-1)(k+1)) from C11, and c2 from any code with distinct rows. Fits give slopes .72 at (64, 7) and .217 at (64, 14), against c1 = .111 and .052. The exact constant is open.

verdicts.statement: Three limits of this run
verdicts.gaps: (1) and (2) are correct readings of the proof and of t7_pack.py. (3) is a prediction and has no check. I add a stronger form of (3) for C4: it is 0 unless the order matrix has sign rank above k + 1 and at least (k+1)^2 rows and pairs carry weight.
verdicts.corrected_statement: As stated.

verdicts.statement: Blocked-by claim: the entry limit gives m/k while fits grow faster than m, and the bound does not reach 1 at k = K/2
verdicts.false_step: Two parts. Fits do not grow faster than m in order: at fixed K, k, L/e is at most affine in m (see C12). The failure to reach 1 at K = 2k is a fault of the Lewis dual with |T| <= 1, not of the entry limit as such.
verdicts.counterexample: K = 64, k = 32. A projector dual reaches ratio .990 at m = 100. The cause in C10: with 1 in the range and uniform x, T_ci >= -(r-2)/r, so |T| = 1 is not reached on the negative side, and only the negative side needs the domain limit.
verdicts.gaps: The first blocker stands: blocks are not coupled. It is the real one. This is what fine-scale sharing needs, and neither my complement nor the projector form removes it.
verdicts.corrected_statement: The exponent of m is right in C11. The remaining gap on the level table is a factor in c(K, k), which is .24 at K = 64, k = 14, tending to 1 at K = 2k with the projector form. The real block is coupling between blocks.

What survives as use: C10 and its projector complement are correct lower bounds on L_free that hold for every competitor span and name no build, for free codes, table, read and box. C4 and C4.1 survive after the kept-unit and own-family fixes. C6 is a correct limit on C3-type bounds on exact level trees. C12 is refuted and its route is closed. The missing piece stays the coupling between blocks.
